# Custom Fightwear Artwork: MMA and BJJ Production Guide
Prepare custom fightwear artwork for MMA shorts, BJJ rash guards and team kits with file formats, logo placement, seam checks, color approval and a supplier-ready checklist.
By TONTON · Published November 21, 2026 · 8 min read
IN THIS GUIDE
What should a custom fightwear artwork package include?Which file format is best for sublimated MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards?How should you map logos onto MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards?How do you design artwork for team kits and private-label collections?What competition and permissions should you check before approval?How do you approve color, scale and the physical sample?Custom fightwear artwork checklist for a supplier quoteKey takeawaysBuyer questionsDiscuss your specification →THE SHORT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Custom fightwear artwork is production-ready when the supplier has editable logos, defined colors, a panel-by-panel placement map, seam and safe-zone instructions, label requirements, and a final revision number. Buyers should approve both the digital mockup and a physical sample because screen color, artwork scale and seam alignment do not prove how the finished MMA shorts or BJJ rash guard will look. TONTON’s official artwork guidance recommends vector files where available, panel placement instructions, and mockup plus sample approval before bulk production.

Printed panel layout at the TONTON factory. Panel boundaries, orientation and seam allowances belong in the production artwork review.

## What should a custom fightwear artwork package include?
A supplier-ready package should contain more than one logo file. Send a structured folder with:
TONTON’s artwork-for-sublimation resource lists vector AI, EPS, SVG or editable PDF as preferred logo inputs where available. It also recommends identifying panel placement, color references, safe zones and seam alignment before the final production file is approved.

- Product direction: MMA fight shorts, 2-in-1 grappling shorts, rash guard, training shorts or team kit.

- Intended use: training, academy membership, competition, retail, private label or a mixed program.

- Editable artwork: vector logos and editable files where available.

- Color direction: brand references, named colors and any non-negotiable color requirements.

- Placement map: front, back, sleeve, side panel, waistband, liner and label positions.

- Hierarchy: primary logo, secondary mark, sponsor marks and optional graphics.

- Technical notes: seam alignment, bleed, safe zones, repeat elements and areas where text must not be distorted.

- Size and quantity plan: styles, colorways, adult/youth ranges and quantities by size.

- Labels and packaging: neck label, care label, hangtag, barcode, polybag or other packing requirements.

- Revision control: approved artwork version, date and person responsible for sign-off.

- artwork-for-sublimation resource →

## Which file format is best for sublimated MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards?
Vector artwork is usually the best starting point for logos, lettering and simple marks because it can be resized without becoming pixelated. Adobe describes vector artwork as scalable for logos and brand graphics. A file extension alone does not establish that artwork is vector or editable; confirm the actual objects, embedded images, fonts and linked assets. For textures or photographic-style graphics, use a high-resolution raster file at the intended production size.
Do not enlarge a small screenshot and assume it is production-ready. A low-resolution file may show jagged edges or lose detail when placed across a large short panel. If the original artwork is unavailable, ask the designer to rebuild the important logo elements as editable vector artwork rather than relying on a blurry reference.
Which file format is best for sublimated MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards?Artwork type | Useful input | Main check before production |
Brand or sponsor logo | AI, EPS, SVG or editable PDF | Confirm fonts, outlines, transparency, colors and permission to use the mark. |
Pattern or texture | High-resolution raster or editable layered file | Confirm resolution at final size, repeat direction and panel bleed. |
Team name and numbers | Editable text or outlined vector | Check spelling, font ownership, minimum size and distortion across seams. |
Photo-based graphic | High-resolution raster | Check resolution, contrast and whether the image is licensed for apparel use. |
Mixed design | Organized layered source file plus exported preview | Label layers and identify which elements are mandatory, optional or reference-only. |

## How should you map logos onto MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards?
Start with the garment pattern, not a blank rectangle. Production artwork must follow the garment panel layout. Confirm the factory’s printing, transfer and cutting sequence; a graphic can change when it crosses a side seam, waistband, sleeve join or high-stretch area.
Use a panel map with these fields:
For a rash guard, inspect the chest, upper back, sleeves, side panels, neckline and lower hem. For fight shorts, inspect the front panels, back rise, side split, waistband, gusset, liner and any hook-and-loop or drawcord area. Keep small sponsor logos away from locations where a seam or fold could make them unreadable.
The custom sublimated rash guard page and custom BJJ and MMA shorts page are useful starting points for separating artwork decisions from fit, fabric, waistband, liner and size-grading decisions. A graphic mockup does not replace a garment specification.

- Panel name: front left, front right, back, side, sleeve, waistband or liner.

- Artwork element: academy crest, sponsor logo, team name, number or pattern.

- Priority: must appear, may appear or reference only.

- Orientation: upright when worn, repeated, mirrored or continuous.

- Safe zone: minimum distance from seams, hems, openings and closures.

- Scale rule: fixed size, proportional size or size-grade adjustment.

- Approval note: what must be checked on the mockup and physical sample.

- custom sublimated rash guard page →

- custom BJJ and MMA shorts page →

## How do you design artwork for team kits and private-label collections?
Build a visual system that survives more than one order. Define the core logo, team identifier, sponsor zone, approved colors, graphic style and label system. Keep these rules consistent when the garment changes from a rash guard to fight shorts or a high-split 2-in-1 style.
For private-label collections, separate the permanent brand identity from seasonal graphics. The high-split 2-in-1 grappling shorts reference can help buyers discuss shell, liner, side-split and waistband decisions before placing final artwork.

- high-split 2-in-1 grappling shorts reference →

## What competition and permissions should you check before approval?
Separate artwork approval from competition approval. The IBJJF uniform requirements state that no-gi shirts and rash guards must be skin-tight, cover the torso to the shorts’ waistband and follow specified color directions. The page also gives requirements for shorts, including length, pockets, drawstrings, zippers and potentially risky plastic or metal elements. These are event-specific rules, not universal approval for every organization or division, so recheck the relevant organizer before bulk production.
Permissions matter too. The U.S. Copyright Office distinguishes copyright in creative works from trademark protection for words, symbols and designs identifying goods or services. The USPTO explains that a business name or logo may function as a trademark. Confirm that the gym, sponsor, artist or brand has authorized the artwork for production and resale.
Do not call a kit “competition legal,” “official” or “approved” without support from the exact garment, division and event rule set.

- IBJJF uniform requirements →

- U.S. Copyright Office →

- USPTO →

## How do you approve color, scale and the physical sample?
Use two stages:
1. Approve the digital mockup
Check spelling, hierarchy, orientation, panel placement, color references, sponsor order, labels and the relationship between garments. Record the revision number.
2. Approve the physical sample
Check the worn garment under normal lighting and realistic movement. Review color, logo scale, seam and stretch interaction, rash guard coverage, shorts waistband and liner, labels, packaging, measurements and tolerances.
A monitor is not proof of printed color. TONTON’s artwork guidance recommends physical sample confirmation because color, scale and seam interaction can differ from a screen mockup. Save the sample photos, measurement chart, material record and final artwork for repeat orders.

## Custom fightwear artwork checklist for a supplier quote
Before requesting a quote, confirm the following:
TONTON’s sampling and MOQ guide explains that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, while the applicable minimum depends on style, design, colorway, size allocation and project requirements. Use the written quotation and approved specification as the commercial reference.
Custom fightwear artwork checklist for a supplier quoteQuestion | Buyer decision |
Garment and use? | Product type, construction and intended use. |
Quantity? | Total units plus style, color and size breakdown. |
Mandatory artwork? | Primary logo, team name, sponsors and labels. |
Editable files? | AI, EPS, SVG, editable PDF or suitable raster. |
Placement? | Panel map, safe zones and orientation. |
Approval record? | Final mockup, physical sample, revision number and sign-off. |

- sampling and MOQ guide →

## Key takeaways

- Custom fightwear artwork is a production specification, not only a logo or digital mockup.

- Send editable artwork, color references, panel placement, safe zones, labels, quantities and a revision number.

- Design around seams, side splits, waistbands, sleeves and stretch zones before approving the graphic.

- Approve both the digital layout and a physical sample.

- Check current event rules separately from brand design approval.

- Confirm permission to use every sponsor, academy, artist and brand mark.

- Keep the approved sample and specification as the reorder reference.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Before you approve the next step
What is the best file format for custom fightwear artwork?
Vector artwork such as AI, EPS, SVG or a genuinely editable PDF is generally preferred for logos and text. Check that the file contains editable vector objects, with fonts outlined or supplied as agreed. High-resolution raster artwork can work for textures or photographs at the intended production size.
Do I need final artwork before requesting a quote?
No. A supplier can usually discuss a product direction using logos, references and a placement idea. Final production artwork is needed before print and bulk approval, so identify what is confirmed and what is still exploratory.
How should sponsor logos be placed on MMA shorts?
Create a panel-by-panel map with sponsor priority, orientation, scale and safe zones. Keep small marks away from side splits, seams, folds and high-stretch areas, then confirm readability on the physical sample.
Can I use a screenshot of my logo?
A screenshot may help communicate the design direction, but it is not always production-ready. Ask for the original editable or vector file, or have the logo rebuilt before approval.
Does a mockup prove that the final color will be correct?
No. A mockup controls layout and hierarchy, but screen color is not proof of printed color. Approve important colors on the physical sample under normal viewing conditions.
Can one artwork file be used for both a rash guard and fight shorts?
The brand system can be shared, but the production files usually need separate panel layouts. Rash guards and shorts have different seams, stretch directions, openings, labels and size grading.
Can custom fightwear artwork be used in competition?
Only after the exact garment is checked against the current rules of the relevant organization, event, division and category. Training or retail artwork should not automatically be described as competition-approved.
What should a private-label seller keep for repeat orders?
Keep the approved artwork version, editable source files, color references, measurement chart, tolerances, material and construction notes, labels, packaging details, sample images and written sign-off. This reduces ambiguity when a style is reordered.

# Custom No-Gi BJJ Uniform: A Competition Specification Guide for Gyms and Brands
Learn how to specify a custom no-gi BJJ uniform, from IBJJF checks and rash guard fit to shorts, artwork, sampling, care labels and reorder control.
By TONTON · Published November 20, 2026 · 9 min read · Updated November 23, 2026
IN THIS GUIDE
What should a custom no-gi BJJ uniform include?How do you check the rules before designing a competition kit?Officially confirmed fact vs. general development adviceHow should you specify the custom BJJ rash guard?What should you check on the rash guard sample?Which grappling shorts construction should you choose?What artwork and branding information should a team provide?What should the sampling and MOQ checklist contain?How should private-label brands handle labels and care claims?When is a custom no-gi BJJ uniform ready for bulk approval?Key takeawaysBuyer questionsDiscuss your specification →THE SHORT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A custom no-gi BJJ uniform combines a rash guard and grappling shorts with coordinated artwork and separate garment specifications. Define the intended event and rule edition first, then approve fit, materials, seams, measurements, labels and a physical sample. Keep the approved size chart, artwork revision and quantity allocation for bulk production and reorders.

Customer-supplied garment reference. This photograph illustrates fit and team branding; it does not establish approval for an IBJJF event.

## What should a custom no-gi BJJ uniform include?
A practical custom kit normally includes two linked garments:
The two pieces should look like one team system, but they should not be treated as one identical construction. A rash guard needs next-to-skin stretch, seam comfort, and torso coverage. Shorts need secure waist control and movement through shots and scrambles.
TONTON supports the development of custom sublimated rash guards and BJJ/MMA shorts as separate product specifications while coordinating artwork, colors, sponsor placement, labels, and packaging.

- A close-fitting rash guard with an agreed sleeve length, body coverage, fabric direction, seam construction, artwork, and size chart.

- Grappling shorts or compression shorts with an agreed length, waistband, closure, pocket treatment, side opening, liner, and logo placement.

## How do you check the rules before designing a competition kit?
First, identify the exact event, division, gender category, and rule set. A gym’s training uniform can be more flexible than a competition uniform, and one organization’s requirements may not apply to another.
The IBJJF uniform page describes elastic, close-fitting rash guards that cover the torso to the shorts waistband, with specified base and rank colors. For men’s shorts, it gives a half-thigh-to-knee length range and restrictions on pockets, exposed drawcords, zippers, buttons and hazardous hard parts. Check the complete division-specific wording before approving the garment.
Rule timing matters. As checked November 20, 2026, IBJJF also publishes a separate 2027 change notice effective January 1, 2027. Record the event date and applicable edition in your artwork and sample approval. An announced future change is not the rule for every current event.

- IBJJF official uniform requirements →

- IBJJF changes effective January 1, 2027 →

## Officially confirmed fact vs. general development advice
Officially confirmed fact vs. general development adviceTopic | Evidence status | What to do |
No-gi rash guard coverage and permitted color directions | IBJJF requirement on its official uniform page | Compare final artwork and coverage with the current rule set. |
Shorts length, pockets, exposed drawstrings, zippers, and hard components | IBJJF requirement on its official uniform page | Remove or secure features that conflict with the applicable rules. |
Fabric weight, fiber blend, seam type, and hem grip | Project-specific development choices | Confirm composition, GSM, stretch, recovery, and finishing on the sample. |
“Competition-ready” wording | Not a universal certification | Use only after the specific event and approved garment have been checked. |
Care instructions | Market and garment compliance matter | Use instructions supported by evidence for the finished garment. |

## How should you specify the custom BJJ rash guard?
Start with the user and movement pattern rather than the graphic. A team that trains several times a week may need a different fit and seam priority from a lifestyle-oriented private-label brand.
Record these decisions in the brief:
TONTON’s custom rash guard development page identifies a supplied 220 GSM, 85% polyester / 15% spandex reference for one product direction, while making clear that final composition, weight, hand feel, and stretch are confirmed for the selected project. One reference specification should not be copied into every style without approval.

- Short sleeve or long sleeve

- Adult, youth, or separate women’s fit direction

- Chest, torso, shoulder, sleeve, and hem measurements

- Desired compression level and stretch direction

- Fabric composition and weight to be confirmed for the selected style

- Flatlock or other seam construction to be reviewed on the sample

- Optional mesh placement, if required and appropriate for the design

- Optional silicone hem grip, including width and placement

- Neck label, care label, sponsor marks, and packaging

- custom rash guard development page →

## What should you check on the rash guard sample?
Wear-test the garment through pummeling, shrimping, bridging, framing, and repeated overhead movement. Check whether the neckline stays comfortable, the torso remains long enough, the sleeves restrict reach, and seams feel smooth against the skin. If a hem grip is included, check ride-up, skin contact, stretch, and wash performance before approving it as a selling point.
Do not describe a mesh panel as “breathable” in a technical or tested sense unless you have evidence for that claim. A mesh appearance shows construction; it does not prove a measured moisture or airflow result.

- Review the sample approval checklist →

## Which grappling shorts construction should you choose?
Choose shorts according to use, coverage, and rule constraints before finalizing the artwork. The following comparison is a development framework, not a claim that one style is best for every athlete.
TONTON’s high-split 2-in-1 grappling shorts reference shows one direction using a four-way-stretch outer shell and a supplied 250 GSM milk-silk liner reference. Confirm the actual liner composition, weight, length, waistband system, side split, and event suitability on the approved project sample.
Which grappling shorts construction should you choose?Construction | Suitable for | Advantages to review | Not ideal when |
Outer fight shorts | MMA, striking, BJJ training, and flexible team programs | Branding surface, adjustable waist, and freedom around the legs | You need built-in close coverage or a competition-specific compression layer. |
High-split 2-in-1 shorts | Grappling, wrestling-influenced movement, and training programs | Outer-shell mobility with an inner compression layer | The event prohibits a feature, liner fit is wrong, or length conflicts with rules. |
Longer grappling shorts | Buyers prioritizing thigh coverage and a conservative training fit | More coverage and a straightforward team silhouette | The athlete needs a shorter, high-mobility cut. |
Compression shorts under shorts | Training and permitted competition combinations | Close fit underneath and a coordinated base layer | Color, length, or combination conflicts with the organizer’s rules. |

- high-split 2-in-1 grappling shorts reference →

## What artwork and branding information should a team provide?
A strong artwork pack reduces revisions and makes repeat orders easier. Provide vector logo files, brand colors, academy and sponsor hierarchy, front/back/sleeve/side-panel placements, event restrictions, label artwork, packing requirements, and the final artwork revision number.
Review artwork at panel seams, side openings, sleeve joins, waistbands, and curved areas. A design that looks correct on a flat mockup may need adjustment when it is cut and assembled. Keep the approved mockup and physical sample together; the image alone does not define fit or construction.

## What should the sampling and MOQ checklist contain?
Before asking for a quote, prepare the same information for every supplier:
TONTON’s sampling and MOQ guide states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, while also explaining that the applicable minimum depends on style, design, colorway, size allocation, and project requirements. Its advertised 3–7 day sample target begins after usable artwork and product details are confirmed; sourcing, new patterns, and revisions can change the schedule. Use the written quotation, not a generic starting number, as the commercial reference.

- Product type and construction

- Intended use: training, academy membership, competition, retail, or private label

- Quantity by style, color, and size

- Adult/youth or men’s/women’s fit requirements

- Artwork status and logo files

- Fabric and construction priorities

- Labels, packaging, and barcode requirements

- Destination country and target delivery date

- Sample requirements and expected revision rounds

- Inspection points and wash-test requirements, if applicable

- sampling and MOQ guide →

## How should private-label brands handle labels and care claims?
Private-label sellers should treat labels as part of product compliance and customer experience. Confirm fiber content, country-of-origin requirements, brand identity, size information, care instructions, and market-specific obligations with the responsible compliance professional or importer.
For covered U.S. apparel, FTC guidance calls for attached care instructions supported by a reasonable basis. Review the finished garment and its components when agreeing washing, drying and ironing directions. Consult the official rule and compliance guidance for the product and market.
For sublimated or dark-colored fightwear, agree any required test method and acceptance criteria before making durability claims. AATCC TM15 summarizes acid-perspiration colorfastness testing; a published method is not proof that this garment was tested or that it resists every kind of fading.

- FTC Care Labeling Rule →

- clothing care-label compliance guidance →

- AATCC TM15 summary →

## When is a custom no-gi BJJ uniform ready for bulk approval?
Bulk approval should happen only after the buyer can answer “yes” to all of the following:
Use the TONTON project builder to submit a brief with product type, estimated quantity, intended use, size range, delivery country, target date, and available artwork or reference files.

- Does the garment match the intended rule set and event check?

- Are measurements and tolerances written down?

- Does the sample remain comfortable during realistic grappling movement?

- Are artwork scale, colors, seams, and sponsor placements approved?

- Are fabric composition, weight, stretch, recovery, and finishing confirmed?

- Are labels and care instructions supported by project evidence?

- Are quantities by style, color, size, and packaging clear?

- Is the sample revision, artwork version, and size chart saved for reorders?

- TONTON project builder →

- Plan quantities by garment and size →

## Key takeaways

- A custom no-gi BJJ uniform is a specification system, not just a matching print.

- Check current event rules before approving rash guard colors, torso coverage, shorts length, pockets, drawstrings, zippers, and hard components.

- Treat the rash guard and shorts as coordinated but separate constructions.

- Approve a physical sample for fit, movement, seams, materials, artwork, labels, and finishing.

- Record the final measurement chart, tolerances, artwork revision, material record, packaging, and care instructions for repeat orders.

- Use supplier starting points such as MOQ and sample timing as project-specific inputs, not universal promises.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Before you approve the next step
What is a custom no-gi BJJ uniform?
A custom no-gi BJJ uniform is a coordinated rash guard and grappling-short system developed around a team or brand identity. It should include confirmed fit, materials, construction, artwork, sizing, labels, and intended-use requirements rather than only a printed graphic.
Can a training kit be used in an IBJJF competition?
Not automatically. Training apparel may include design or construction details that do not match current competition rules. Check the official IBJJF requirements and the specific event’s inspection guidance before relying on a kit for competition.
How long should no-gi BJJ shorts be?
For IBJJF men’s no-gi shorts, the official uniform page says they should cover at least halfway down the thigh and be no longer than the knee. Other organizations may differ, so verify the applicable rule set before finalizing the pattern.
Should a rash guard be tight or loose for no-gi BJJ?
A competition-style no-gi rash guard is generally close-fitting and made from elastic material. The final fit should allow full movement without excessive looseness, restricted reach, uncomfortable seams, or insufficient torso coverage.
Are 2-in-1 grappling shorts suitable for every competition?
No. A 2-in-1 construction can be useful for training and grappling movement, but liner color, length, waistband details, side split, and other features must be checked against event rules. Approve the exact garment, not only the product category.
What is a reasonable starting MOQ for custom BJJ gear?
A starting MOQ is project-specific. TONTON states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, but the applicable minimum must be confirmed by style, design, colorway, size allocation, and other requirements in the quotation.
Do custom BJJ rash guards need care labels?
Care-label obligations depend on the market and product. For U.S. apparel, the FTC Care Labeling Rule requires covered manufacturers and importers to provide care instructions, and those instructions need a reasonable basis for the finished garment.
What should I send a manufacturer for a custom team uniform quote?
Send garment types, intended use, quantity by size and color, artwork or logos, fit direction, construction priorities, destination country, target date, labels, packaging, and sample expectations. A complete brief produces a more useful project-specific quote.

Home/Blog/Fightwear Buying GuideFightwear Buying Guide

# Custom MMA and BJJ Fightwear Sizing: How to Build a Reliable Size Set
Build a reliable custom MMA and BJJ fightwear sizing system with measurement points, size grading, team allocation, sample checks and production tips.
By TONTON · Published November 19, 2026 · 10 min read
IN THIS GUIDE
What is the best way to plan custom MMA and BJJ fightwear sizing?Why can’t one size chart be used for every fightwear product?How do you create a custom MMA and BJJ fightwear size chart?Define the fit directionChoose body measurements and garment measurementsBuild grading between sizesMatch the chart to the target marketTest representative sizes physicallyWhat should a gym collect before ordering a team size set?Which is better for a private-label brand: body sizing or garment sizing?What should be checked on a fightwear sizing sample?How should competition requirements affect a custom size set?What should be included in a manufacturer brief?Key takeawaysBuyer questionsDiscuss your specification →THE SHORT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
The best approach is to build the size system around the garment’s use, not around labels such as S, M or L. Measure the intended customer group, separate rash guard and short requirements, define consistent measurement points, create a size chart, and test representative samples before bulk production. For a team order, collect quantities by product, colorway, adult or youth range and size rather than using one shared chart for every garment.

Finished-garment review: check agreed measurement points and fit against the approved size chart.

## What is the best way to plan custom MMA and BJJ fightwear sizing?
A size label is only a shorthand. The useful information is the measurement behind it, the fit intention and the tolerance the manufacturer will follow.

## Why can’t one size chart be used for every fightwear product?
A compression rash guard and an MMA short solve different fit problems. A rash guard needs close torso coverage, controlled stretch and comfortable sleeve and neck dimensions. Shorts need secure waist retention, usable leg opening, appropriate coverage and freedom through kicks, sprawls, shots and ground movement.
The same athlete may choose different labelled sizes in the two products. This is not automatically a problem; it is a reason to publish clear, product-specific measurements.
Why can’t one size chart be used for every fightwear product?Product | Main sizing priority | Measurements to define | Sample movement check |
Close-fit rash guard | Controlled compression and torso coverage | Chest, waist, body length, shoulder, sleeve length and hem circumference | Reach, rotation, hand-fighting and repeated raising of the arms |
Outer MMA fight shorts | Waist security and leg mobility | Waist, hip, outseam, leg opening, side split and rise | Kicks, sprawls, shots and stance changes |
2-in-1 grappling shorts | Shell mobility plus inner-layer coverage | Waist, hip, outseam, liner length, leg opening and split height | Scrambles, seated guard, bridges and hip rotation |
Training shorts | Daily comfort and repeat wear | Waist, hip, outseam, rise and leg opening | Warm-up, conditioning and normal gym movement |
Team kit | Consistency across a group | Product-specific chart plus adult/youth separation | Fit review on more than one representative body type |

## How do you create a custom MMA and BJJ fightwear size chart?
Use five steps: define the fit, choose measurement points, agree size grading, match the chart to the market, and approve representative physical samples. Keep each product’s measurement method and tolerance with its final size chart.

## 1. Define the fit direction
Write down whether the garment should be close fit, athletic fit or relaxed fit. “Performance fit” is too vague on its own. For a rash guard, state whether the torso should sit close to the body and whether the hem should be extended or use an optional grip. For shorts, state the preferred waist feel, leg length, side opening and coverage.
Separate adult and youth requirements. A youth team range should not be created by simply scaling down an adult garment without checking proportions, movement and safety requirements.

## 2. Choose body measurements and garment measurements
Body measurements help a wearer select a size. Garment measurements help the buyer and manufacturer control the finished product. A practical chart should identify both where possible.
For a rash guard, start with chest, waist, shoulder width, sleeve length and center-back length. For shorts, start with relaxed waist, extended waist, hip, outseam, rise, leg opening and side-split height. Identify how each point is measured—for example, whether the waist is measured relaxed, stretched or at a specified point on the garment.
Define whether each garment value is a flat half-width or a full circumference. For raglan sleeves, specify the sleeve-length starting point because a conventional shoulder seam may be absent. For elastic waists, agree the relaxed and extended measurement procedure rather than comparing measurements taken under different tension.
Do not mix inches and centimeters in the same approval sheet without clearly labelling the unit. Use one primary unit for production and provide a conversion only for customer convenience.

## 3. Build grading between sizes
Size grading is the planned change from one size to the next. It should not be treated as a guess or as a universal industry formula. The grading direction depends on the pattern, fabric stretch, fit, product category and target market.
For a private-label range, ask for a full chart rather than only one sample size. Review whether chest, waist, hip, length and opening changes remain proportionate across the range. A size chart that works at the middle size may create tight armholes at the top size or excessive body length at the smaller size.

## 4. Match the chart to the target market
North American and European customers may use different expectations for labels, units and fit. Choose the primary market before finalizing the chart. Display body-measurement guidance in the customer-facing size chart, while keeping detailed garment measurements in the technical specification.
For an online seller, include a clear instruction such as “measure around the fullest part of the chest” or “measure the waist where the waistband will sit.” Avoid telling a buyer to choose their usual size without showing the measurement basis.

## 5. Test representative sizes physically
A digital mockup can confirm artwork and layout, but it cannot confirm fit, stretch recovery, hand feel, seam comfort or finished dimensions. TONTON’s sampling guidance also separates mockup review from physical sample review and recommends confirming the approved sample and specification before bulk work.
For a new product, consider testing a middle size and one size near each end of the intended range. For a team kit, include representative members with different heights, builds and fit preferences rather than asking one athlete to approve the entire range.

## What should a gym collect before ordering a team size set?
A gym or academy should collect the following information in a simple spreadsheet:
Flag uncertain sizes for a try-on or measurement review. Separate “size selected from chart” from “size confirmed after sample” so the buyer can record what changed and why.

- Athlete or member reference, if needed for internal allocation

- Product type: rash guard, MMA shorts, grappling shorts or training shorts

- Adult or youth range

- Preferred size based on the approved chart

- Chest, waist, hip or other required measurement where the fit is uncertain

- Quantity by size, colorway and product

- Competition or training use

- Notes about unusually long torso, larger thigh, broad shoulder or preferred ease

- Allocate quantities by garment and size →

## Which is better for a private-label brand: body sizing or garment sizing?
A private-label brand needs both, but they serve different purposes. Body sizing is easier for the shopper to understand. Garment sizing is more useful for product development, quality control and repeat orders.
The most dependable system connects the two. If a private-label brand changes the fabric, liner, waistband, sleeve length or pattern, it should review the chart again rather than assuming the old size information still applies.
Which is better for a private-label brand: body sizing or garment sizing?Use case | Primary reference | Why it matters |
Online product page | Body measurements plus fit notes | Helps a customer choose a size without handling the garment |
Factory specification | Garment measurements and tolerances | Creates a measurable production reference |
Team order | Body measurements and quantity allocation | Reduces mismatches across different body types |
Reorder | Approved garment chart and sample | Preserves continuity with the previous production |
New fabric or pattern | Body chart plus new garment measurements | Confirms that a material or construction change has not altered fit |

## What should be checked on a fightwear sizing sample?
Use a written checklist, not only a visual impression:
AATCC’s official standards directory lists methods covering areas such as colorfastness to perspiration, crocking and laundering. These are testing references, not automatic claims that a particular custom garment has passed a test. If testing is required, specify the method, sample, laboratory and acceptance criteria in writing.

- Measurements: Check every agreed point against the chart and tolerance.

- Fit: Try the garment in a neutral stance and in sport-specific movement.

- Coverage: Check torso, waistband, liner and leg coverage during movement.

- Security: Confirm the waistband, drawcord, hem or optional grip remains comfortable and stable.

- Seams: Inspect seam placement, stretch, thread ends and skin contact.

- Artwork: Check graphics, logos and labels after the garment is worn and stretched.

- Wash and care direction: Confirm the final care copy matches the approved material and intended market.

- Record keeping: Save the approved chart, sample photos, measurement points, tolerance, artwork version and revision date.

- Use the sample approval checklist →

## How should competition requirements affect a custom size set?
Competition use should be treated as a separate approval track. A training garment that fits well may still require review against the rules of a specific event, federation or host authority. IMMAF states that national federations may use their own rule sets, while world-championship competition follows IMMAF rules and protocols. Use the official rules entry point to find the current documents for the intended competition.
Before approving a competition-oriented design, confirm the current official requirements for garment type, branding, colors, closure, coverage and permitted equipment with the relevant organizer. Do not describe a custom garment as competition-approved unless that approval is documented for the applicable event and version of the rules.
For European private-label sales, also review textile labelling obligations. Regulation (EU) No 1007/2011 addresses textile fibre names and fibre-composition labelling for products made available on the EU market. Final labels should be checked for the destination market and product configuration rather than copied from an unrelated sample.

## What should be included in a manufacturer brief?
A production-ready custom MMA and BJJ fightwear sizing brief should include:
TONTON’s project form asks buyers to provide the product, estimated quantity and intended use, with size range and destination country available as additional project information. TONTON’s custom shorts and rash guard pages also state that selected projects start from 10 pieces, while the applicable minimum should be confirmed by style, design, colorway and size allocation.

- Product category and intended sport

- Fit direction and target customer

- Target market and measurement units

- Body size chart and garment measurement chart

- Measurement method and tolerances

- Adult/youth and men’s/women’s requirements where applicable

- Quantity by product, colorway and size

- Fabric, liner, waistband, sleeve, hem and split requirements

- Artwork version, label copy and packaging direction

- Sample sizes to be reviewed

- Required delivery country and target date

- Competition-use notes and the rule source to be checked

- Prepare your sizing brief →

## Key takeaways

- Custom MMA and BJJ fightwear sizing should be built by product type, fit direction and target market—not by labels alone.

- Rash guards, MMA shorts, 2-in-1 grappling shorts and training shorts need different measurement points.

- A team size allocation should separate adult/youth, product, colorway and size quantities.

- A physical sample is required to confirm fit, movement, coverage, seams and finished measurements.

- Competition rules, textile labelling and testing requirements must be checked against current official sources and the destination market.

- Keep the approved chart, tolerances, sample, artwork version and quote together for repeat orders.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Before you approve the next step
Should MMA shorts and BJJ rash guards use the same size chart?
No. Use separate product-specific charts because shorts and close-fit rash guards have different construction and movement requirements. They can share a label system, but the measurement points and fit notes should remain distinct.
What is the most important measurement for a rash guard?
Chest is a key starting measurement, but it is not enough by itself. Check waist, body length, shoulder, sleeve length, hem and torso coverage on the physical sample.
What is the most important measurement for fight shorts?
Waist security is usually the first check, followed by hip, rise, outseam, leg opening and side-split height. The correct priority depends on the product construction and intended movement.
Can a digital mockup confirm fightwear sizing?
No. A digital mockup can help confirm artwork and layout, but it cannot confirm stretch, recovery, hand feel, seam comfort, opacity or finished measurements. Use a physical sample for sizing approval.
How many sizes should a team sample before a bulk order?
Sample a representative middle size and sizes near the ends of the planned range; add more fit checks when the team includes adult and youth members or a wide range of body types. The exact sample plan should follow the product and order risk.
Should private-label brands publish body measurements or garment measurements?
Publish body measurements with clear measuring instructions for shoppers, and retain garment measurements with tolerances in the technical file. Using both creates a bridge between customer selection and production control.
Are TONTON’s advertised minimums universal for every size set?
No. TONTON states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, but the applicable minimum depends on the agreed style, design, colorway, size allocation and project requirements. Confirm the project-specific quotation before planning inventory.

# How to Choose Custom MMA and BJJ Fightwear Fabric and Fit
Learn how to choose custom MMA and BJJ fightwear by comparing fabric, fit, construction, competition requirements and sample checks.
By TONTON · Published November 18, 2026 · 8 min read · Updated November 19, 2026
IN THIS GUIDE
How do you choose custom MMA and BJJ fightwear?What should you define before choosing fightwear fabric?Which fabric direction suits custom rash guards?Which shorts construction is better for MMA and BJJ?How do you check fit for combat movement?Are custom fightwear designs automatically legal for competition?What should a buyer request from a fightwear supplier?How can fabric claims be made more precise?What should teams approve before bulk production?Buyer questionsDiscuss your specification →THE SHORT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Custom MMA and BJJ fightwear should be selected by intended use, fabric behavior, fit, coverage, closure security, construction and event requirements. Compare rash guards, unlined shorts and lined shorts separately. Approve a physical sample, measurement chart, artwork version and project-specific quote before bulk production; a digital mockup cannot verify comfort, opacity or movement.

Printed rash guard fabric reference: compare texture, stretch, opacity and fit on the selected sample.

## How do you choose custom MMA and BJJ fightwear?
The right custom MMA and BJJ fightwear depends on where it will be used, how the athlete moves, what coverage is required, and whether the garment is for training, team identity, retail or a specific competition. Start by defining the use case, then compare fabric stretch and recovery, fit, waistband or hem security, seam comfort, artwork placement and size grading. For competition projects, check the current rules of the event organizer before approving the design.
A professional-looking mockup is useful, but it cannot confirm hand feel, opacity, stretch recovery, seam comfort or finished measurements. Those decisions require a physical sample and a written specification.

## What should you define before choosing fightwear fabric?
“Performance fabric” is not one universal specification. A fabric’s fiber content, weight, knit or weave, stretch direction, recovery, surface feel, opacity and printing compatibility can all affect the finished garment.
For a custom fightwear brief, record these points:
TONTON’s custom rash guard development reference identifies polyester-spandex performance directions, sublimation compatibility, flatlock seam options and an optional silicone hem grip. The exact composition, fabric weight and construction still need to be confirmed for the selected project and approved sample.

- Intended activity: MMA striking, wrestling, no-gi grappling, BJJ drilling, strength training or mixed gym use.

- Layering: Single-layer shorts, 2-in-1 shorts with a liner, short-sleeve rash guard or long-sleeve rash guard.

- Stretch direction: Note whether the garment needs two-way or four-way movement through kicks, sprawls and ground transitions.

- Coverage: Define torso length, liner length, side opening, leg coverage and opacity when stretched.

- Moisture expectations: Use measurable requirements where needed; do not treat the word “quick-dry” as a laboratory result.

- Print and branding: Confirm whether sublimation, labels, sponsor marks, private labels or packaging are required.

## Which fabric direction suits custom rash guards?
A close-fit rash guard normally needs a fabric direction that supports stretch, recovery, next-to-skin comfort and artwork clarity. A supplied TONTON product reference lists 220 GSM and an 85% polyester / 15% spandex blend for one sample direction; that should not be treated as a universal specification for every custom rash guard.
When reviewing a rash guard sample, check:
For teams and academies, separate adult and youth size blocks should be reviewed rather than assuming that one grading system will fit every wearer.
Rash guard fabric and fit sample checksCheck | Why it matters | What to record |
Stretch and recovery | The top must move with the athlete without becoming loose during wear | Stretch direction, recovery after movement and agreed tolerance |
Opacity | Artwork and coverage can change when the fabric is stretched | Visual check in the intended size and movement position |
Seam finish | Low-profile seams can affect skin comfort during repeated grappling | Seam location, stretch, thread security and inside-surface feel |
Hem behavior | A close fit can ride up during inversions and scrambles | Body length, hem circumference and optional grip placement |
Artwork alignment | Panel joins can change how logos and graphics appear | Mockup version, panel map, logo scale and print approval |

## Which shorts construction is better for MMA and BJJ?
There is no single best construction for every athlete or buyer. The choice depends on movement, coverage, personal preference, competition requirements and whether the product is intended for training or retail.
TONTON’s high-split grappling short reference combines a four-way-stretch outer layer, a stated 250 GSM milk-silk compression liner, an ultra-high side split, adjustable drawstring, anti-slip silicone grip strip and reinforced stitching. The page also states that final fit, graphics, sizing and movement performance are checked on the approved sample. Buyers should confirm the liner’s composition and all project-specific measurements in writing.
Compare custom fightwear construction by intended useConstruction | Suitable for | Advantages to review | Less suitable when |
Single-layer fight shorts | Striking, mixed training and buyers who prefer a lighter shell | Simple construction, open movement and flexible visual design | The wearer wants built-in compression coverage or a longer inner layer |
2-in-1 high-split shorts | MMA, grappling, wrestling and high-mobility training | Outer leg clearance plus a fitted inner layer for coverage and support | The buyer wants a loose short, no liner or a lower side opening |
Training shorts | Gym, conditioning and general combat preparation | Adaptable everyday use and a less competition-specific look | The event has specific equipment or uniform requirements |
Coordinated shorts and rash guard | Academies, teams and private-label collections | Consistent identity, sponsor placement and repeatable color direction | The two garments are assumed to share the same fit or fabric without separate approval |

## How do you check fit for combat movement?
A fightwear fit check should reproduce the movement the garment is meant to support. A standing try-on alone is not enough.
Use this sample checklist:
Record the results on the sample specification. If the side split, waistband, liner length, fabric, sleeve or size chart changes, request confirmation of whether a new sample is needed.

- Rash guard: Raise both arms, rotate the torso, reach forward and simulate a seated or grounded position. Check torso coverage, neckline comfort, sleeve length and hem movement.

- Single-layer shorts: Walk, squat, kick, sprawl and rotate. Check side-opening height, crotch comfort, waistband holding and leg coverage.

- 2-in-1 shorts: Check the shell and liner separately and together. Confirm that the liner does not pull against the shell during a wide stance or ground transition.

- All garments: Inspect seams, thread ends, labels, logo position, print clarity, measurement tolerance and wash-test requirements.

## Are custom fightwear designs automatically legal for competition?
No. A custom design is not automatically competition-approved. Rules vary by organization, division, gender, rank, event and date. The IBJJF uniform information should be checked for the relevant competition, and athletes should follow the latest official rules and organizer instructions.
For an academy or private-label project, separate the commercial design brief from the competition compliance check. You can develop a strong team identity for training and retail while reserving a rule-compliant colorway or construction for a particular event. Do not describe a garment as competition legal unless the relevant authority has confirmed it for that use.

## What should a buyer request from a fightwear supplier?
A useful quote should connect the product idea to an inspectable specification. Request:
TONTON’s sampling and MOQ guide states that selected custom projects start from 10 pieces, while the applicable minimum depends on the product, material, construction, artwork, quantity mix and project requirements. It also states a 3–7 day sample target after usable artwork and confirmed details, with sourcing, new patterns and revisions potentially changing the schedule. Treat these as project-planning references, not universal promises.

- Product type and intended use

- Outer fabric and liner direction, including composition and weight where confirmed

- Measurement chart, size grading and tolerances

- Waistband, hem, sleeve, split and seam construction

- Artwork files, panel map, logo placements and color references

- Labels, packaging and private-label requirements

- Quantity by style, design, color and size

- Sample charges, development scope and sample timing

- Production timing, shipping basis and destination assumptions

- The conditions that apply to repeat orders

## How can fabric claims be made more precise?
Turn a claim such as “quick-dry” into an agreed requirement before sample approval. Record the fiber composition, GSM, intended use and conditioning or washing procedure, then agree the applicable test method, laboratory and acceptance criterion when a numerical performance claim matters. A visual demonstration is not a laboratory report.
Ask for the report for the actual fabric or garment and confirm the sample identity, test date, method and result. A published test method does not establish that a TONTON product has passed it. Keep the approved material record with the physical sample for reorders.

## What should teams approve before bulk production?
Use a five-part approval gate:
The custom fightwear project builder can be used to organize product type, estimated quantity, intended use, size range, destination and artwork status before the quotation stage.

- Product: correct garment type, layer structure and intended use

- Fit: measurements, grading, tolerances and movement checks

- Material: composition, weight, stretch, recovery, opacity and care information

- Branding: artwork version, panel placement, color references, labels and packaging

- Order: size-by-size quantity, MOQ, quote scope, timing and shipping basis

- Use the team size and quantity planner →

- Build a custom fightwear project brief →

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Before you approve the next step
What is the most important decision when ordering custom fightwear?
Start with intended use. MMA striking, no-gi grappling, academy training and retail may require different coverage, movement, construction and compliance checks.
Is a higher GSM fabric always better for fightwear?
No. Fabric weight must be balanced with stretch, opacity, hand feel, drying expectations, climate and the garment’s intended use. Confirm the selected fabric rather than choosing by GSM alone.
Are 2-in-1 grappling shorts suitable for MMA training?
They can be, when the shell, liner, split and waistband suit the training movement. Confirm liner length, coverage, side-opening height and fit on a physical sample.
Should a team order one universal size ratio?
No. Build the quantity from a confirmed member or customer list where possible. Record quantities by garment, style, color and size, and ask the supplier to confirm the grading and minimums.
Can a digital mockup replace a sample?
No. A mockup helps review artwork and logo placement, but it cannot confirm fit, material behavior, opacity, seam comfort or workmanship.
Can a custom rash guard be advertised as competition legal?
Only after checking the current rules of the specific organization and event. A product page or supplier statement alone does not establish competition approval.
What should private-label brands keep for reorders?
Keep the approved sample and written specification. Store the artwork version, measurements, tolerances, material record, labels, packaging instructions and any approved corrections.

# Custom MMA Team Kits: A Buying Guide for Gyms, Academies and Fightwear Brands
Plan custom MMA team kits with practical guidance on shorts, rash guards, rules, artwork, sizing, samples, MOQ and OEM/ODM production.
By TONTON · Published November 17, 2026 · 9 min read · Updated November 19, 2026
IN THIS GUIDE
What are custom MMA team kits, and what should they include?How do you choose the right custom MMA team kit structure?Which shorts and rash guard combination should you choose?How do you check whether a custom MMA team kit is competition-ready?What artwork and branding details should a team prepare?How should you plan sizes, quantity and MOQ?What should you test before approving the sample?What should you send a manufacturer for a custom MMA team kit quote?Key takeawaysBuyer questionsDiscuss your specification →THE SHORT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Custom MMA team kits are coordinated sets of fight shorts, rash guards and optional training apparel. Plan the use case, construction, event requirements, size allocation and shared artwork before approving physical samples. Confirm MOQ and timing for each product and colorway before bulk production. Matching graphics alone do not make a kit competition-approved.

Customer-supplied coordinated kit reference: align the top and shorts artwork while approving each garment separately.

## What are custom MMA team kits, and what should they include?
Custom MMA team kits are coordinated fightwear sets that use a shared color system, logo treatment and artwork across products such as MMA fight shorts, grappling shorts, rash guards and training pieces. A practical kit normally has a competition-oriented or training-oriented short, a matching rash guard when the team needs a complete upper layer, and optional training shorts or team apparel for daily gym use.
The right kit is determined by the wearer and the use case. A competition team may prioritize event-specific color and equipment requirements. A gym uniform may prioritize repeat ordering, mixed sizes and easy member onboarding. A private-label brand may need repeatable measurements, labels, packaging and a clear retail size range.
TONTON’s website presents a custom MMA team kit reference combining a rash guard and shorts with coordinated sublimation artwork. That is a useful starting structure, but each team should still approve its own construction, artwork, size breakdown and event requirements.

## How do you choose the right custom MMA team kit structure?
Start with one sentence that defines the first buyer and the moment of use. For example: “This kit is for an amateur MMA team that needs coordinated training and event apparel for adult athletes.” That sentence helps prevent a training uniform from being described as competition-approved without verification.
This comparison is a planning framework, not a guarantee of event eligibility. “Training kit,” “teamwear” and “competition kit” should remain separate labels in the product brief until the relevant organizer confirms the requirements.
Choose a custom team kit by use caseTeam situation | Recommended kit direction | Main decision | Less suitable approach |
MMA gym uniform | Custom fight shorts plus optional rash guard | Consistent identity, durability checks and repeat sizes | Designing only one sample size |
Amateur fight team | Shorts and rash guard planned around the target rule set | Corner color, identification marks and prohibited details | Assuming one rule set applies to every event |
BJJ academy with MMA crossover | Rash guard plus grappling or MMA-style shorts | Coverage, movement and no-gi requirements | Copying an MMA kit without checking grappling rules |
Private-label fightwear brand | Hero short, matching rash guard and training piece | Repeatable fit, labels, packaging and SKU control | Launching many styles before the core fit is approved |
E-commerce seller | One coherent kit story with a manageable size range | Inventory risk, product photography and size guidance | Offering colors and sizes that are not production-ready |

## Which shorts and rash guard combination should you choose?
Choose the product combination by testing the movement and coverage requirements of the end user.
Custom MMA or BJJ shorts should be reviewed for waist security, rise, leg opening, split height, stretch direction, seam quality and artwork placement. A team should test stance changes, sprawls, kicks, shots, guard transitions and scrambling rather than judging the shorts only while standing. If a 2-in-1 construction is under consideration, inspect the outer shell and inner liner separately for ride-up, twisting, pressure and coverage.
Custom rash guards should be reviewed for fit, sleeve length, body length, neckline, opacity under stretch, seam comfort and artwork alignment. Confirm the exact fabric composition and weight for the selected style. The TONTON website lists a rash guard reference using 220 GSM fabric and an 85% polyester / 15% spandex composition; treat this as a product reference to confirm for the selected project, not as a universal specification for every order.
Use the custom sublimated BJJ and MMA shorts and custom sublimated rash guards pages as starting points for comparing product directions. The final team kit should be approved from a written specification and physical sample.

- custom sublimated BJJ and MMA shorts →

- custom sublimated rash guards →

## How do you check whether a custom MMA team kit is competition-ready?
The short answer is: check the exact event, division, association and current rule version before sampling and again before production.
The IMMAF 2026 Adult MMA Competition Rules and Procedures summary says the listed equipment, including rash guards and shorts, must follow the assigned red or blue corner; approved gold kit may be used where the full rules permit. This is a non-controlling summary. The full rules, authorized procedures and event instructions take priority.
The UWW International Amateur MMA Rules and Regulations, August 2025 provides another example of event-specific requirements, including short-sleeve close-fitting rash guards, corner-color requirements and restrictions on details such as pockets, zippers and metal components for competition shorts. These rules apply to UWW-recognized international amateur MMA events; they are not a universal standard for every gym or promotion.
For no-gi BJJ, the IBJJF Uniform Requirements set separate conditions for rash guards and shorts, including fit, color, coverage and potentially hazardous garment details. A kit that is appropriate for MMA training may not meet IBJJF requirements.
Do not use “competition legal,” “approved,” or “official” in product copy until the relevant authority has confirmed the exact garment and event conditions.

- Target event, association and division

- Current rulebook or official uniform page

- Corner, belt or team-color requirement

- Sleeve, length and coverage requirement

- Pocket, zipper, metal, buckle or exposed-cord restrictions

- Athlete name, country code, sponsor or identification placement

- Approval contact or official uniform-check process

- Date on which the requirements were last checked

- IMMAF 2026 Adult MMA Competition Rules and Procedures summary →

- UWW International Amateur MMA Rules and Regulations, August 2025 →

- IBJJF Uniform Requirements →

## What artwork and branding details should a team prepare?
A production-ready team kit brief should separate the visual concept from the manufacturing instructions. Prepare vector logos where available, brand colors, sponsor marks, athlete names or numbers, artwork placement, preferred base colors and any restrictions on logo size or position.
The goal is not to place every logo on every panel. The goal is to make the team identifiable while keeping marks readable on a moving athlete and manageable for repeat production.

- Front, back, side and sleeve layout for each garment.

- A shared color system that remains identifiable across shorts and rash guards.

- A clear hierarchy for team crest, sponsor marks, athlete names and manufacturer label.

- Safe areas around collars, hems, splits, seams and waistband joins.

- Separate artwork files for outer shorts, liners, rash guards and packaging.

- A version number so the approved artwork can be reused for team replenishment.

- Written confirmation of who owns the supplied logos and sponsor artwork.

## How should you plan sizes, quantity and MOQ?
Give the manufacturer the total quantity and a quantity-by-size breakdown for every product, colorway and design. “One hundred sets” is not enough if the supplier does not know whether the order contains adult sizes only, youth sizes, separate short and rash guard allocations, or different athlete names.
TONTON’s homepage states that selected styles start from 10 pieces and that the target sample window is 3–7 days after product details and usable artwork are confirmed. The same page notes that final MOQ, timing and price depend on the selected project. Confirm the exact breakdown through the custom fightwear sampling and MOQ guide rather than treating a headline MOQ as a promise for every construction.

- Product and construction for each item

- Adult, youth or mixed size range

- Body measurements or approved garment measurements

- Quantity by size, product and colorway

- Athlete names, numbers or individualized artwork

- Labels, hangtags, packaging and folding requirements

- Destination market and required delivery window

- Target event date, if applicable

- Sample size and wear-test participants

- Reorder plan and approved tolerance record

- custom fightwear sampling and MOQ guide →

## What should you test before approving the sample?
A digital mockup can confirm the general artwork direction. It cannot confirm finished fit, seam comfort, opacity, waistband behavior or movement clearance. Have representative athletes wear the sample during the movements and training conditions that matter to the team.
For textile testing and quality-control methodology, the American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists (AATCC) is a professional reference point. AATCC is not a fight-sports approval body, so textile testing guidance does not replace event uniform inspection.

- Waistband security and drawstring comfort

- Short length, split height and leg clearance

- Rash guard body length, sleeve length and torso recovery

- Liner coverage and ride-up, if using a 2-in-1 short

- Seam contact during ground work and repeated movement

- Color, logo scale and panel alignment

- Size-chart measurements versus the physical garment

- Wash-care instructions and appearance after testing

- Rule-specific details for the target event

- American Association of Textile Chemists and Colorists (AATCC) →

## What should you send a manufacturer for a custom MMA team kit quote?
Send a concise brief rather than a single product photo. Include the kit structure, intended use, target quantity, sizes, artwork status, desired construction, destination and timing. Add the rule-check information if the garments may be used at a named event.
TONTON’s Project Builder is the appropriate next step for organizing this information. A clear brief allows the supplier to confirm the customization route, missing specifications, sample plan, selected MOQ and project-specific schedule.

- Project Builder →

## Key takeaways

- Custom MMA team kits should be planned as a coordinated system of shorts, rash guards and optional training pieces.

- Choose the kit around training, academy teamwear, private-label retail or a named competition—not around graphics alone.

- Confirm current event rules before using “competition-ready,” “approved” or similar claims.

- Approve a physical sample with representative athletes before bulk production.

- Give the manufacturer quantities by size and product, not only a total set count.

- Keep the final artwork, measurements, labels and quality notes as the team’s reorder specification.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Before you approve the next step
What is usually included in a custom MMA team kit?
A typical kit can include custom MMA fight shorts and a matching rash guard, with optional grappling shorts, training shorts or team packaging. The final mix should reflect whether the kit is for training, academy identity, competition or retail.
Are custom MMA team kits automatically legal for competition?
No. Competition eligibility depends on the exact event, division, association and current rule version. Check the official requirements for color, coverage, sleeves, closures, sponsor marks and approval procedures before production.
Should a gym choose a matching rash guard and shorts?
Usually, a matching set is useful when consistent team identity and coordinated photography matter. A gym may choose separate products when members train in different sports, when a rule set requires a specific garment, or when budget and inventory need to be staged.
How many custom MMA team kits should a gym order?
Order planning should start with the active roster, expected new-member demand, size distribution and reorder timing. Give the manufacturer a size-by-size allocation and confirm the selected style’s MOQ rather than using a universal quantity assumption.
What should a team test on a sample?
Test fit, movement clearance, waistband security, seam comfort, opacity, print alignment, size-chart accuracy and any event-specific garment restrictions. A mockup alone cannot verify these physical characteristics.
Can private-label brands use the same team kit structure?
Yes, but a retail brand needs additional controls for repeatable measurements, labels, packaging, SKU naming, photography and customer size guidance. A gym team order and a private-label product should not automatically use the same approval checklist.
What information is needed for a custom fightwear quote?
Provide the product mix, construction direction, estimated quantity, size range, artwork or logo files, target colors, destination market and required timing. If an event is involved, add the official rule source and the date it was checked.
