PRODUCT DIRECTION

## Build a rash guard around the way your customers train.

A strong custom rash guard program starts with use, fit, and artwork—not a generic blank garment.
TONTON supports brands, BJJ academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams, and distributors with product development for custom sublimated rash guards. We help define sleeve length, panel direction, size requirements, fabric performance, artwork placement, and packaging before the order moves forward.

01

### BJJ & grappling academies
Create a consistent team identity across adult, youth, rank, or competition programs.

02

### MMA gyms & fight teams
Develop training apparel around movement, repeat wear, and clear sponsor placement.

03

### Private-label brands
Translate a brand direction into a repeatable rash guard range with coordinated colors and graphics.

PRIVATE LABEL / SPECIFICATION & SAMPLE CHECKS

## Compare your custom rash guard specification
Choose the sleeve, material and finishing as one garment. These are development options, not specifications shared by every product.
Development choices and approval checks for your custom orderDecision | Development direction | Check on the physical sample |
Sleeve and fit | Short sleeves or long sleeves; adult and youth measurements approved separately. | Shoulder reach, chest fit, sleeve length and torso coverage. |
Fabric | 220 GSM, 85% polyester / 15% spandex is one supplied reference. Other product weights and blends need separate confirmation. | Composition, GSM tolerance, opacity under stretch, recovery and hand feel. |
Seams and ventilation | Flatlock seam direction; optional mesh at the underarm or side body. | Seam stretch, skin contact, panel joining and mesh placement. |
Hem | Extended torso or an optional silicone anti-slip band, depending on the selected style. | Body length, grip placement, skin comfort and movement in a wear trial. |
Sublimation and labels | Panel artwork, academy colors, sponsor graphics, neck labels and packaging. | Print scale, panel alignment, color reference, label content and agreed wash tests. |

### Agree the sample, quotation and reorder reference
Send quantity by size and color, artwork or reference images, delivery country and target date. Confirm materials, labels, packaging, sample charges and shipping basis in the quote. Selected projects start from 10 pieces; minimums apply by the agreed style and design.
Sampling targets 3–7 days after details and usable artwork are confirmed. Sourcing and revisions may extend timing. Retain the approved sample, measurement tolerances, artwork version and material record; reconfirm availability when reordering.

### Check the evidence
See a supplied US customer's repeat-order records, specification conversations and Alibaba feedback. Private details are withheld; completed and pending orders are distinguished.

CUSTOMIZATION OPTIONS

## What can be customized on a sublimated rash guard?
Each decision is reviewed together so the visual design and garment construction support the same end use.
01

### Sleeve and fit direction
Choose short or long sleeves and define the intended fit and size range for your market.

02

### All-over artwork
Apply team colors, patterns, logos, names, and sponsor graphics across the printable panels.

03

### Fabric performance
Review stretch, hand feel, weight, and intended training conditions before sampling.

04

### Construction details
Confirm panel layout, breathable mesh, flatlock seam direction, neckline, silicone hem grip, printed labels, and other brand-specific requirements.

PERFORMANCE CONSTRUCTION

## Inspect the fabric, seams, mesh, and finishing details.

Real sample photography shows the product areas a buyer should review before approving a custom sublimated graphic Rash Guard for BJJ, MMA, grappling, or training.

Fabric direction
Polyester-spandex stretch performance fabric

Ventilation option
Underarm and side mesh panel

Seam direction
Low-profile flatlock construction

Hem option
Silicone anti-slip grip

Compare actual sample details for custom BJJ rash guards: mesh panels, flatlock seams and an optional silicone gripper hem. These construction choices can be specified for private-label academy and brand orders. Click a detail photograph to inspect the full image.
01

### Performance fabric and panel fit
The complete sample shows a smooth stretch body, raglan sleeve direction, close neckline, and clean areas for custom sublimated graphics or logos.

02

### Mesh panel and body-fabric seam
A real sample close-up shows open mesh joined to smooth body fabric. Specify underarm or side placement, coverage and opacity; approve the mesh and seam stretch together.

03

### Flatlock seam close-up
The photograph shows the low-profile seam on the sample fabric. For custom BJJ rash guards, review the skin-side finish, seam stretch and recovery on a fit sample; confirm the stitch specification before bulk production.

04

### Multi-panel seam junction
This close-up shows several seam lines meeting at a panel junction. Inspect alignment, bulk, thread ends and comfort during movement when approving your custom compression top.

05

### Silicone gripper hem option
The inside-hem photograph shows a glossy grip strip beside the mesh panel and finished edge. An optional silicone gripper can help limit ride-up; confirm width, placement, stretch, skin contact and wash performance on the approved sample.

06

### Tagless printed neck label
The physical sample shows an 85% polyester and 15% spandex fabric label printed inside the neck. Composition and care copy are finalized for each approved project.

## Specify the construction before approving your rash guard sample.
Send the mesh placement, seam finish and silicone hem requirements with your artwork and size allocation. Review these details together with stretch mesh options, the rash guard fabric and construction guide and the sampling and MOQ guide.

FABRIC DIRECTION

## Rash Guard fabric should balance stretch, recovery, and print clarity.
We commonly evaluate polyester-spandex performance directions for sublimated Rash Guards. Final composition, weight, hand feel, and stretch are confirmed against the approved sample and project requirements.

### Multi-directional stretch
Supports close-fit movement for BJJ, MMA, grappling, and training applications.

### Shape recovery
Helps the garment return toward its intended fit after repeated movement and wear.

### Smooth print surface
Supports clear gradients, detailed graphics, sponsor marks, and team colors.

### Project-specific GSM
Fabric weight is selected and confirmed during development instead of being presented as one universal specification.

RASH GUARD CRAFT

## How a sublimated Rash Guard moves from artwork to inspection.
01

### Artwork and color preparation
Logos, pattern scale, sponsor marks, and panel placements are organized in the digital mockup.

02

### Sublimation transfer
Approved artwork is transferred into compatible performance fabric for an integrated, lightweight graphic result.

03

### Panel cutting
Printed pieces are cut to the approved pattern with artwork position and panel direction in view.

04

### Stretch-garment sewing
The neckline, sleeves, body panels, and hems are assembled using construction suited to the selected stretch fabric.

05

### Finished-garment inspection
Measurements, seams, visual placement, color, labeling, and workmanship are reviewed before packing.

OEM / ODM PROCESS

## From your idea to an approved custom product.
A practical OEM route for custom BJJ and MMA rash guards, with key decisions confirmed before bulk work begins.
See the detailed service process →
01

### Define the product brief
Share the rash guard style, sleeve length, fit direction, quantity, and target user.

02

### Review artwork and options
Send logos, brand colors, references, and feature requirements so the mockup and specification can be prepared.

03

### Confirm the sample
Review fit, material, construction, color, branding, and functional details before bulk work begins.

04

### Produce, inspect, and deliver
Production follows the approved details, followed by finished-garment inspection, packing, and shipment preparation.

### 3. Check documented order evidence
Customer records describe their own products and experience. They do not establish identical materials, results or commercial terms for another project.
Inspect a documented rash guard and shorts repeat order →

What must the sample and quotation confirm?
Minimum order
Selected projects start from 10 pieces. Confirm minimums per style, design and colorway, and the permitted size mix.

Sample route
The 3–7 day target starts after usable artwork and details are confirmed. Agree sample charges, revisions, sourcing and the actual schedule.

Size allocation
Use the selected pattern’s measurement chart. Keep adult/youth and tops/shorts separate; retain the approved sample and chart version.

Written quote
Confirm unit and sample costs, decoration, labels, packaging, shipping basis, destination and delivery assumptions before approval.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom rash guard questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01Can our academy order custom jiu jitsu rash guards with different names and rank colors?
Send a single roster with the exact name spelling, size, sleeve length, fit direction and artwork variant for each athlete. TONTON reviews the pattern and print layout before confirming the order. Identify rank-color variants separately, and check the rules for the named event and division. Confirm how each style, design and colorway affects the minimum in the written quotation.
02What should a private-label rash guard brand approve before launching?
Approve the intended customer and fit, selected fabric, transferred print colors, logo placement, seam finish, hem details, labels and packaging on a representative physical sample. Record measurements and tolerances, artwork revision and quantity by size. Agree care and testing requirements separately and retain the approved references for reorders.
03Can we design custom jiu jitsu rash guards for an academy or club?
Yes. Use your academy logo, team colors and approved artwork to develop custom jiu jitsu rash guards in short- or long-sleeve cuts. Specify size allocations, names or sponsor marks, fabric direction, seam finish and any hem grip. Review the visual mockup and physical sample before bulk approval.
04Can we develop a matching custom rash guard and grappling shorts set?
Yes. A coordinated no-gi kit can share colors, graphics and sponsor placement across the rash guard and shorts. Each garment needs its own fabric, cut, size chart and construction approval; matching artwork does not mean identical materials or sizing. Send quantities and sizes separately for both pieces.
05How do we start a bulk custom rash guard order for our brand?
Choose a product reference and send the design direction, estimated quantity, size breakdown, destination and target date. TONTON reviews OEM or ODM development, material availability, labels, packaging and sampling requirements before quoting. Selected projects start from 10 pieces, with the minimum per style, design and colorway confirmed in writing.
06Can we mix sizes within a custom order?
Mixed-size allocations can be reviewed within an agreed style, design and colorway. Send quantities for each size and identify adult or youth ranges. Confirm the minimum per style and colorway, measurement chart and any separate pattern or sampling requirements in the written quotation; a 10-piece starting quantity does not automatically apply across multiple designs.
07What should the quotation include before we approve an order?
Confirm the garment specification, quantities by size and color, decoration method, labels, packaging, sampling charges, shipping basis and destination. Ask which items are included or priced separately, and whether duties or taxes are included in the agreed delivery terms. Production and dispatch timing should be recorded against the approved sample and project requirements.
08Can you develop private-label rash guards with our neck labels and packaging?
Yes. Specify the logo method, neck-label content, hem branding, size and care labels, and individual packing requirements in your brief. Review label feel, print placement and the packing specification with your sample; these details can affect the quotation and minimum quantity.
09How should we check a rash guard sample for a repeat order?
Approve numerical measurements and tolerances, sleeve and torso fit, fabric stretch and recovery, artwork alignment, seam comfort and any silicone hem grip. Agree wash-test requirements and keep the approved garment, artwork revision, material record and size chart as the reorder reference. Reconfirm material availability before each repeat order.
10What information should I send for a custom rash guard quote?
Send the required quantity, short- or long-sleeve preference, target users, size range, artwork or logo files, and any reference products. These details help us define the development brief and confirm the next step.
11Can TONTON make rash guards for BJJ academies and MMA teams?
Yes. We support custom rash guard programs for BJJ academies, MMA gyms, grappling teams, brands, and distributors. Team colors, sponsor marks, names, and coordinated designs can be reviewed during artwork development.
12What is the MOQ for custom sublimated rash guards?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure is confirmed against the style, size breakdown, artwork, and other project requirements.
13Can I customize both long-sleeve and short-sleeve rash guards?
Yes. Sleeve length is one of the first product decisions. We can review short- and long-sleeve directions, along with fit, panel layout, sizing, and artwork placement.
14Will sublimated graphics peel or create a heavy print layer?
Sublimation transfers the artwork into compatible performance fabric rather than adding a thick surface print. It is suited to detailed, all-over graphics and avoids a heavy printed layer on the garment.
15Can I review a mockup and sample before bulk production?
Yes. A digital mockup is used to review the visual direction, and sample development can be used to confirm fit, construction, color, and branding before bulk production.
16Which artwork files are best for production?
Vector logo and artwork files are preferred because they support clean scaling and placement. Brand colors, fonts, sponsor marks, and reference images are also helpful when preparing the mockup.
17What fabric is used for a custom Rash Guard?
A Rash Guard is typically developed with a smooth polyester-spandex performance fabric selected for stretch, recovery, print compatibility, and next-to-skin comfort. The exact fiber ratio and fabric weight are confirmed for the selected project rather than assumed from a generic specification.
18How is a sublimated Rash Guard manufactured?
After the artwork and color direction are approved, the design is transferred into compatible fabric, the printed panels are cut, stretch seams and the neckline are assembled, and the finished Rash Guard is inspected for workmanship, measurements, color, and branding.
19Where can mesh panels be placed on a custom BJJ rash guard?
Underarm and side-panel mesh options can be reviewed for your design. The sample photograph shows the mesh-to-body seam. Confirm coverage, opacity, stretch compatibility and seam comfort; a mesh appearance alone does not establish tested breathability.
20How do we check flatlock seams before bulk production?
Inspect the skin-side seam finish and multi-panel junctions, then assess seam stretch, recovery, thread security and comfort during movement. Record the approved stitch specification and fit sample for repeat orders.
21Can private-label rash guards have a silicone gripper hem?
Yes, an optional inside silicone grip can be reviewed during sampling. Specify grip width and placement, hem circumference and stretch, then check skin contact, ride-up during movement and wash performance before approval.
22Can a custom Rash Guard include mesh panels, flatlock seams, and a silicone hem grip?
Yes. These construction directions can be reviewed during development. Mesh placement, seam type, hem finish, and anti-slip silicone grip should be confirmed against the intended fit, fabric, and approved sample before bulk production.

Custom Rash Guard: material, fit and procurement decisionsMaterial record | Blue Team and White Logo references: 220gsm, 85% polyester / 15% spandex. The Samurai reference lists 220gsm; confirm its fiber ratio separately. These specifications do not automatically apply to every custom option. |
Measurements and fit | Specify sleeve length, adult or youth fit, chest, body length and sleeve measurements. Agree a measurement method and numerical tolerances on the approved size sheet; a market label alone does not define fit. |
Customization scope | Review panel artwork, logos, neck labels and optional silicone hem grip. Confirm the selected hem construction and artwork version on the sample. |
Evidence behind this direction | Published product specifications, actual garment and seam photographs, silicone-hem detail footage and separately identified customer production references. |
Starting quantity | Selected custom projects start from 10 pieces. Confirm the minimum per style, design and colorway; 10 pieces is not a promise that different products or unrelated designs share one minimum. |
Mixed sizes | Send a separate quantity-by-size list for each garment. Adult / youth patterns, tops / shorts and colorways need an explicit allocation; do not assume any mix is automatically accepted. |
Sample timing | The advertised 3–7 day target starts after usable artwork and product details are confirmed. New patterns, material sourcing, revisions or special finishing can change the schedule. |
Quote scope | Request the unit and sample charges, artwork or development scope, labels, packaging, shipping basis and destination in one written quote. No universal price or free-sample entitlement is implied. |
Approval and repeat orders | Keep the approved sample version, artwork, materials, size chart, tolerances and packing instructions. Recheck material availability, MOQ and timing when reordering. |

## One training short for gym, combat conditioning, outdoor movement, and utility wear.

This is a multi-purpose functional short—not a single-purpose MMA competition short.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom training shorts questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01What should we confirm for custom training shorts with zip pockets?
Specify what the pocket must hold, the opening direction, location and closure. Review access, seam reinforcement and comfort on the physical sample during the intended exercise. For contact training, assess exposed hardware separately and follow the activity or organizer requirements rather than assuming a gym pocket design is suitable.
02How should a private-label training shorts sample be approved?
Compare the sample with your measurement chart, fabric and liner specification, waist adjustment, pockets, ventilation, logo placement and labels. Record fit and finishing corrections and agree the relevant wash and movement checks. Keep the signed-off specification and sample reference for bulk production and reorders.
03How do we choose between training shorts and MMA or BJJ shorts?
Start with the intended use and construction. Gym or running projects may prioritize pockets, ventilation and everyday storage; combat projects should review shell coverage, split height, liner, waistband security and exposed hardware. Product names alone do not establish competition suitability. Compare the physical sample against your movement needs and any applicable event requirements.
04Does every training short include a compression liner?
No. Our product references include different inner constructions, including mesh trim and separate or integrated inner layers. Confirm whether you need an unlined shell, partial mesh lining or a fitted two-in-one compression short, then approve coverage, inner-leg length, seams and fit on the sample.
05Can we mix sizes within a custom order?
Mixed-size allocations can be reviewed within an agreed style, design and colorway. Send quantities for each size and identify adult or youth ranges. Confirm the minimum per style and colorway, measurement chart and any separate pattern or sampling requirements in the written quotation; a 10-piece starting quantity does not automatically apply across multiple designs.
06What should the quotation include before we approve an order?
Confirm the garment specification, quantities by size and color, decoration method, labels, packaging, sampling charges, shipping basis and destination. Ask which items are included or priced separately, and whether duties or taxes are included in the agreed delivery terms. Production and dispatch timing should be recorded against the approved sample and project requirements.
07What should I send to start a functional training shorts project?
Share the intended use, quantity, target fit, preferred length, size range, logo files, reference products, and required features such as a zip pocket, perforated ventilation, adjustable waist, or specific stretch direction.
08Can you make custom gym shorts for a private-label brand?
Yes. We support OEM and ODM development for fitness brands, gyms, teams, retailers, and distributors. The project can include custom fit direction, materials, colors, labels, and logo placement.
09What is the MOQ for custom training shorts?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure depends on the selected style, color and size breakdown, artwork, and construction requirements.
10Can I customize the waistband, zip pockets, ventilation, and reinforcement?
Yes. These are connected development decisions. Their placement and construction are confirmed during product review so they can be recorded in the mockup, specification, and sample.
11Which logo method is best for this woven short?
The suitable method depends on the approved fabric, artwork, stretch, and placement. Heat transfer, screen print, film print, or selected embroidery directions can be reviewed before sampling; final wash and stretch performance should be checked on the approved sample.
12Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. Sample development allows your team to check fit, movement, material, waistband, workmanship, and branding before the approved specification moves into bulk production.
13Can the shorts be coordinated with other team apparel?
Yes. Colors, logos, and design language can be developed to coordinate with rash guards, tops, or other teamwear. Each garment is still reviewed according to its own construction and material needs.

## Compare custom MMA and BJJ shorts constructions
A high-split 2-in-1 short is one reference, not the only fight-short construction. Select the shell, coverage and closure before developing the panel artwork. Share event clothing requirements separately for competition projects.
Development choices and approval checks for your custom orderDecision | Development direction | Check on the physical sample |
Outer combat short | A shell-based style with the chosen gusset, length and side opening; a compression liner is not assumed. | Shell stretch, ground-movement coverage, seams and closure security. |
High-split 2-in-1 short | Four-way-stretch outer shell with a compression inner layer. The supplied high-split reference uses a 250 GSM milk-silk liner. | Actual liner composition, weight and length; shell-to-liner fit through kicks and sprawls. |
Split and leg length | Standard or higher side opening and an agreed finished length, subject to pattern review. | Opening height, edge reinforcement, leg coverage and movement. |
Waistband | Elastic, drawcord or hook-and-loop direction; silicone grip only where specified. | Waist measurement, closure holding, cord finish and wearer comfort. |
Branding and packing | Sublimated graphics, sponsor logos, private labels and size-specific packaging. | Artwork at seams, label content, size allocation and agreed wash tests. |

2-IN-1 HIGH-SPLIT CONSTRUCTION

## Support inside. Unrestricted movement outside.

These men's gladiator shorts combine a breathable quick-dry outer layer with a soft, supportive inner compression liner. The ultra-high split is designed for MMA, wrestling, grappling, boxing, and high-intensity gym training.

2-IN-1Athletic shell + compression liner
4-WAYStretch for unrestricted movement
ULTRA-HIGHGladiator side split
ANTI-SLIPSilicone grip + drawstring waist

CONSTRUCTION OVERVIEW

### Review the shell, liner, split, and waistband as one system.
The outer shell uses a thick-yet-lightweight four-way-stretch direction, while the inner layer provides coverage and can carry approved custom artwork.

COMBAT MOVEMENT

## Built for kicks, sprawls, shots, and hard training.

### Freedom without excess fabric
A lightweight four-way-stretch shell moves independently while the inner liner maintains support and coverage.

### Combat-training coverage
The fitted inner layer stays close through striking, wrestling, grappling, and functional training.

OEM / ODM PROCESS

## From your idea to an approved custom product.
A supported route from fight-short concept to an approved BJJ, MMA, or grappling teamwear program.
See the detailed service process →
01

### Define the product brief
Share the BJJ, MMA, or grappling use, fit, length, waistband, quantity, and artwork direction.

02

### Review artwork and options
Send logos, brand colors, references, and feature requirements so the mockup and specification can be prepared.

03

### Confirm the sample
Review fit, material, construction, color, branding, and functional details before bulk work begins.

04

### Produce, inspect, and deliver
Production follows the approved details, followed by finished-garment inspection, packing, and shipment preparation.

### 3. Check documented order evidence
Customer records describe their own products and experience. They do not establish identical materials, results or commercial terms for another project.

What must the sample and quotation confirm?
Minimum order
Selected projects start from 10 pieces. Confirm minimums per style, design and colorway, and the permitted size mix.

Sample route
The 3–7 day target starts after usable artwork and details are confirmed. Agree sample charges, revisions, sourcing and the actual schedule.

Size allocation
Use the selected pattern’s measurement chart. Keep adult/youth and tops/shorts separate; retain the approved sample and chart version.

Written quote
Confirm unit and sample costs, decoration, labels, packaging, shipping basis, destination and delivery assumptions before approval.

BUYER FAQ

## Custom BJJ and MMA shorts questions buyers ask before ordering
Clear answers for brands, gyms, academies, teams, distributors, and private-label buyers.
Read Buyer Resources →Build Your Project Brief →

01How do we customize MMA fight shorts with several sponsor logos?
Send the logos as vector files, the placement priority and any event restrictions. We review scale, panel seams, split openings and visibility in the mockup, then check the printed sample. Confirm that you have permission to use the supplied artwork; a visual reference is not evidence of competition approval.
02Can we order custom MMA shorts for both an academy and a retail brand?
Yes. Academy projects may use shared colors and member size allocations; retail projects may also need a consistent fit block, private labels and packaging. List quantities by style, design, color and size separately. TONTON reviews MOQ, sampling, price and production timing against that breakdown before the order is confirmed.
03Can we mix sizes within a custom order?
Mixed-size allocations can be reviewed within an agreed style, design and colorway. Send quantities for each size and identify adult or youth ranges. Confirm the minimum per style and colorway, measurement chart and any separate pattern or sampling requirements in the written quotation; a 10-piece starting quantity does not automatically apply across multiple designs.
04What should the quotation include before we approve an order?
Confirm the garment specification, quantities by size and color, decoration method, labels, packaging, sampling charges, shipping basis and destination. Ask which items are included or priced separately, and whether duties or taxes are included in the agreed delivery terms. Production and dispatch timing should be recorded against the approved sample and project requirements.
05Should we order outer fight shorts or 2-in-1 lined grappling shorts?
Choose the construction around intended use, coverage and wearer preference. An outer short has a separate shell specification; a 2-in-1 version also needs liner composition, weight, length and joining details. Compare a physical sample for movement, drying, seam comfort and shell-to-liner fit before selecting your production version.
06What quality checks should a private-label MMA shorts sample include?
Review waist and leg measurements, closure security, drawcord finish, split reinforcement, gusset stretch, liner attachment where present, panel print alignment and required labels. Agree a measurement tolerance and wash-test plan. Record corrections on the sample specification and retain the approved version for repeat orders.
07Can TONTON manufacture sublimated MMA shorts for a private-label brand?
Yes. TONTON supports OEM and ODM development of custom sublimated MMA shorts for fightwear brands, gyms and teams. Share the shell and liner direction, fit, size range, graphics, labels and quantity. Artwork placement and material compatibility are reviewed before sampling, and bulk production follows the approved sample and specification.
08What should I compare when choosing a BJJ shorts manufacturer?
Compare intended use, outer-short length, split height, waistband closure, optional liner, fabric direction, stitching, size grading and branding. Request the same specification and quantity breakdown from each supplier, then review a physical sample. Competition requirements should be checked for the intended event rather than assumed from a product name.
09What information is needed for wholesale MMA shorts pricing and repeat orders?
Send the style reference, quantity by color and size, fabric and liner requirements, artwork status, label and packing needs, delivery destination and target date. Keep the approved artwork, size chart, construction notes and sample reference for repeat orders. MOQ, price and lead time are confirmed for the actual project.
10What is the difference between a BJJ shorts project and an MMA shorts project?
The development priorities can differ by preferred fit, length, side movement, waistband, and competition or training use. We start by confirming the intended activity instead of treating every fight short as the same product.
11Can TONTON make matching rash guard and shorts sets?
Yes. Academy colors, logos, sponsor marks, and graphic direction can be coordinated across rash guards and shorts while the construction of each garment is developed separately.
12What is the MOQ for custom BJJ and MMA shorts?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. The final order structure is confirmed after reviewing the style, size and color breakdown, artwork, and construction requirements.
13Can I customize the side split, waistband, length, and inner layer?
Yes. These can be reviewed as part of the product brief. The exact construction is confirmed against the selected style, intended movement, material, and sample requirements.
14Can you place academy logos and sponsor graphics on the shorts?
Yes. Provide vector logos, sponsor marks, brand colors, and placement references. We organize them in the digital mockup so scale, position, and overall balance can be reviewed.
15Can I approve a physical sample before bulk production?
Yes. A sample can be used to review fit, mobility, waistband, material, workmanship, color, and branding before the project is approved for bulk work.
16What should I include in my first inquiry?
Include the product use, target quantity, size range, preferred fit and length, waistband direction, artwork files, reference images, and whether you want matching rash guards or other teamwear.

## Custom black-grey camo rash guard FAQ
Can the camouflage and industrial-style graphics be customized?
Yes. Provide authorized artwork, color references, logo placements and label requirements. Approve the camouflage scale, sleeve layout and chest graphics on an artwork proof and physical sample.
What are the fabric composition and GSM?
Final fiber composition, GSM, stretch and recovery are confirmed for the selected fabric. The supplied brief includes example values rather than a confirmed production specification.
Does the tactical design indicate military or protective certification?
No. Tactical and Spec-Ops describe the visual theme. This training garment is not presented as protective equipment or as military-certified apparel. Abrasion, moisture-management and durability requirements need agreed tests.
Are matching shorts included?
This product reference covers the short-sleeve rash guard. Matching shorts shown in styling photographs are a separate garment and require their own construction, sizing, quotation and sample approval.
Can it be used for No-Gi BJJ competitions?
Confirm the organizer’s current color, coverage, branding and garment rules before specifying a competition version. This reference does not establish event approval.
How do I request MOQ, pricing and a sample?
Send quantity by size, target market, delivery destination, artwork status and required date through the project builder. Confirm MOQ, sample costs, fabric, branding, lead time and packaging against the project brief.

## Custom grey combat shorts FAQ
Can these shorts be customized for a gym or private-label brand?
Send your authorized logo, color references, size range, quantity by size, labels and packaging brief. Confirm branding method and panel placement with an artwork proof and physical sample.
What are the fabric composition and GSM?
Composition, GSM, stretch direction and any ripstop or water-repellent specification require confirmation against the selected fabric and approved sample. The reference photographs do not establish these values.
Is the mesh layer a compression liner?
The reference shows a charcoal micro-dot mesh inner layer. Do not treat it as a fitted compression liner or a two-in-one construction without checking the full liner pattern and sample.
Are these shorts approved for No-Gi BJJ competitions?
Competition acceptance depends on the event rules and approved garment construction. The reference has a visible external drawcord. Check cord exposure, openings, branding, fit and other event requirements before ordering competition garments.
How do I request MOQ, pricing and lead time?
Submit your quantity by size, destination, target delivery date and customization brief through the project builder. MOQ, sample cost, production price and lead time are confirmed after the project specification is reviewed.
What should be checked before bulk production?
Approve a physical sample for waist fit, drawcord retention, split height, mesh coverage, seam comfort, movement and laundering. Confirm fabric composition, GSM, decoration durability and the final care label before bulk approval.

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Custom MMA shorts: materials, colors and order planning.
What is the TONTON Pro Snake-Scale MMA Fight Short?
It is a custom MMA and No-Gi grappling shorts development reference with a scale-pattern shell, hook-and-loop fly, internal drawcord, stretch crotch gusset and curved side openings. Buyers can develop their own colors, logo positions, sizing and labels.
Which colors and SKUs are available as references?
Stealth Black: TT-MMA-SS01-BLK; Tactical Grey: TT-MMA-SS01-GRY; Frost White: TT-MMA-SS01-WHT; Midnight Navy: TT-MMA-SS01-NVY. These website reference SKUs identify color options, not ready-stock inventory. Grey currently has detail photographs rather than a complete front view.
What are the shell and gusset materials?
The supplied brief specifies a 100% micro-polyester shell and an 88% polyester / 12% spandex stretch-knit gusset. Confirm exact GSM, material records and performance on the selected sample before bulk production.
Is the snake-scale effect jacquard or sublimation?
The photographs establish the visible scale-like pattern. They do not determine whether it is jacquard, sublimation or another finish. Approve the chosen material and decoration process with a swatch and sample.
Can these shorts be used for MMA or No-Gi BJJ competition?
Review the actual garment against the organizer’s current equipment rules, including pockets, hardware, exposed hook-and-loop and drawcords. This product page does not certify competition approval.
Are the waistband and seams guaranteed never to slip or tear?
No measured test is supplied for absolute non-slip, tear-proof or lifetime durability claims. Check closure security, elastic recovery, seam strength and mobility with a physical fit sample.
Can a private-label brand customize the design?
Yes. Discuss colors, scale artwork, waist tab, leg emblem, inner labels, pattern dimensions and packaging. Confirm artwork permissions and the final construction before quotation.
How do MOQ, mixed sizes and sampling work?
Selected custom projects start at 10 pieces; minimums per style, design and colorway require confirmation. Send a size allocation and measurement chart. The advertised 3–7 day sample target starts after artwork and details are confirmed; material sourcing, patterns and revisions may extend it.

The supplied close-ups show a purple geometric mesh detail inside the hem. Review its placement and skin contact during sampling.

Inspect the edge stitching and the inside finish for flatness, loose threads and contact with the thigh. The photographs show a sewn finish, not proof of heat-bonded construction.

Specify the vertical wordmark, leg emblem and rear emblem for your own artwork. Confirm whether transfer, TPU or another process suits the fabric; approve stretch and wash checks.

## Custom training & fight shorts: buyer questions
What are these custom training and fight shorts designed for?
They are an OEM/ODM reference for gym training, striking workouts and fightwear collections. Confirm fit and movement on a sample; for BJJ/MMA grappling or competition, review drawcord security, pockets, hardware and event rules separately.
What is the shell composition?
The supplied brief specifies 92% polyester / 8% spandex stretch woven. Exact GSM and measurable stretch, drying, tear and water-resistance properties are not supplied and require a selected material record or test.
Is this a full two-in-one compression liner?
The images show printed mesh at the inside hem. They do not establish a full fitted compression liner. Confirm the inner panel coverage, lining construction and any required two-in-one version during sampling.
Can I customize the blue-purple geometric print and logos?
Yes. Discuss your own colors, geometric artwork, vertical wordmark, emblem, labels and packaging. Confirm print/transfer method, artwork permissions, color matching and wash performance on the approved sample.
What sizes and quantities should I send?
Send waist, hip, rise, outseam, inseam, leg opening and slit-height requirements, followed by quantities per size and colorway. Confirm actual measurements and tolerances rather than relying on a generic 5–7 inch range.
Are the shorts guaranteed tear-proof, non-chafing or permanently colorfast?
No measured test is supplied for those absolute claims. Review seam strength, abrasion, colorfastness, elastic recovery and skin-contact comfort on the selected fabric and physical sample.
What are the minimum order and sample conditions?
Selected custom projects start at 10 pieces. Confirm minimums per style, design and colorway. The advertised 3–7 day sample target begins after artwork and details are confirmed; sourcing, patterns and revisions can change timing.

## White rash guard buying questions
Is this white compression shirt see-through?
Opacity depends on fabric selection, fit, stretch, lighting and moisture. Approve a physical sample in dry and damp conditions, including full movement and body-contour checks. The photographs do not establish a zero-transparency guarantee.
What is the fabric specification?
The supplied development brief specifies 85% polyester / 15% spandex and a target range of 220–250 GSM. Confirm one exact weight, finish and fabric record before bulk production.
Will the seams chafe during BJJ or gym training?
Flat seams are intended to reduce raised contact points. Check the underarm and side seams against the skin during movement; comfort depends on fit and finishing. Zero chafing is not a tested guarantee.
Will the collar stretch out or the hem roll up?
Check neckline recovery and hem position during overhead reaches, bends and repeated washing. Approve the binding, hem length and stitching on the sample; this reference does not establish an anti-roll or anti-deformation test result.
Can I order private label rash guards with my logo?
Yes. Discuss chest and nape artwork, labels, fit and packaging for your OEM/ODM compression shirt project. Selected projects start at 10 pieces; confirm the minimum per style, design and colorway.
How should I choose a size?
The supplied model reference is 5 ft 11 in (180 cm), 195 lb (88 kg), chest 42 in (about 107 cm), wearing MD. Approve actual garment chest, body length, sleeve measurements and tolerances; request a looser fit if needed.
Is the video a fabric performance test?
No. It is a supplied promotional overview. Its stretch demonstration does not measure elastic recovery, opacity, wash durability, compression pressure or recovery benefits.

Buyer FAQ

## Custom Rash Guard questions
Direct answers for brands, academies, gyms and teams preparing a custom order.

01Are Olive, Blue and White separate products?
They are three color SKUs of this custom short-sleeve team rash guard: Olive TT-RG-SS-01-OLV, Blue TT-RG-SS-01-BLU and White TT-RG-SS-01-WHT. Use one shared product page and specify color, sizes and quantities in your brief. The separate White Short-Sleeve Compression Rash Guard remains a different product.
02What is a silicone anti-slip elastic band on a Rash Guard?
It is an elastic band with silicone grip at the inside lower hem. It helps reduce ride-up during BJJ, MMA and grappling movement, but does not guarantee that the garment never moves. Review hem circumference, stretch, grip feel and comfort on the worn sample.
03What should brands specify for a custom Rash Guard with a silicone gripper hem?
Share the intended sport, target fit, size range, band width and position, grip preference and seam-finish requirements. TONTON reviews the silicone anti-slip elastic band with the garment fabric and construction before sample approval. Final dimensions and construction are confirmed for each OEM or ODM project.
04What fabric is used for this custom Rash Guard?
This Rash Guard uses 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra made from 85% polyester and 15% spandex. The fabric has a soft hand feel, high elasticity and opaque coverage.
05Is the fabric see-through when stretched?
The 220gsm fabric is selected for opaque coverage. Fit, stretch recovery and opacity are checked again on the approved sample before bulk production.
06What does the silicone anti-slip elastic band do?
The silicone anti-slip elastic band sits inside the lower hem and helps the Rash Guard stay in position during grappling, drilling and high-movement training.
07Can I customize the colors and logos?
Yes. Colors, logos, sponsor marks, names and panel artwork can be reviewed in the digital mockup before sampling.
08Can this Rash Guard be made for a BJJ academy or MMA team?
Yes. It is developed for custom academy, gym, club, team and private-label programs, including coordinated artwork and size runs.
09Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. The sample is used to confirm fit, material, opacity, construction, artwork placement and branding before bulk production begins.
010What should I send for a quotation?
Send your quantity, target sizes, preferred color, logo or artwork files and any packaging or labeling requirements. We will review the brief and confirm the next step.

The visible specification and physical sample evidence on this page provide the starting point; final measurements, colors and project-specific construction are confirmed before bulk production.

Material & Performance

## Built for close-fit movement without transparent stretch

This long-sleeve Rash Guard uses 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra with a soft hand feel, excellent elasticity and fully opaque coverage. The close-fit fabric supports BJJ, MMA and grappling movement while keeping the black-and-gold artwork crisp.
Recommended for
BJJ academies, MMA teams, grappling clubs, fightwear brands and private-label collections

Customization direction
Black-and-gold all-over sleeve artwork, chest branding, back-neck logo and coordinated team graphics

Performance checks
Fit, stretch recovery, opacity, seam quality and artwork position

Buyer FAQ

## Custom Rash Guard questions
Direct answers for brands, academies, gyms and teams preparing a custom order.

01What fabric is used for the Samurai Rash Guard?
It uses 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra with a soft hand feel, excellent elasticity and fully opaque coverage.
02Is the 220gsm fabric see-through when stretched?
No. The fabric is selected for fully opaque coverage, and opacity, stretch recovery and fit are checked again on the approved sample before bulk production.
03Is this Rash Guard designed for BJJ and MMA?
Yes. The close fit, long raglan sleeves and high-stretch fabric are suited to BJJ, MMA, grappling and other high-movement training.
04Can I customize the sleeve graphics and logos?
Yes. Sleeve artwork, chest branding, back-neck logos, colors and panel graphics can be reviewed in a digital mockup before sampling.
05Can the artwork be produced without a heavy print layer?
Yes. Sublimation integrates compatible artwork into the fabric surface, supporting detailed graphics without a thick raised print layer.
06Can I review a sample before bulk production?
Yes. The sample is used to review fit, opacity, stretch, construction, color and artwork placement before bulk production begins.
07What should I send for a custom quote?
Send the required quantity, size range, logo or artwork files, preferred colors and any labeling or packaging requirements.

## Questions AI tools and procurement teams need answered

01Is the sleeve artwork sublimated?

Buyer FAQ

## Custom grappling shorts questions
Clear answers for BJJ brands, MMA gyms, fight teams and private-label buyers.

01What makes high-split grappling shorts different?
The deep side opening gives the leg more clearance for high kicks, guard movement, scrambling and wide grappling positions without the outer shell pulling across the thigh.
02What fabric is used for these 2-in-1 grappling shorts?
The outer shell uses a reinforced lightweight four-way stretch fabric. The fitted inner layer uses 250gsm milk-silk fabric for substantial coverage and flexible support.
03Can the inner layer use a custom printed pattern?
Yes. The inner compression layer can carry custom colors, patterns, team graphics and brand artwork, subject to artwork and sample approval.
04Are these shorts suitable for BJJ and MMA training?
Yes. The high split, stretch shell and supportive inner layer are developed for kicking, grappling, MMA drills and other high-mobility fight training.
05How does the waistband stay secure during training?
The adjustable waistband combines a drawstring with an anti-slip silicone grip strip to help keep the shorts stable during striking, wrestling and grappling movement.
06Are drying and breathability ratings available for this fabric?
No measured drying-rate or air-permeability results are published for this reference. Request the selected fabric composition, GSM and relevant tests before specifying numerical performance requirements.
07Does this style use a sewn-in clothing label?
The shorts can use a tagless printed label to reduce irritation. Brand, size and care information can be reviewed during product development.
08Which parts of the grappling shorts can be customized?
Buyers can review outer-shell colors, logos, waistband branding, inner-layer artwork, labels and packaging during product development.
09Can I approve a sample before bulk production?
Yes. A sample can be reviewed for fit, split height, movement, materials, construction and artwork placement before bulk production begins.
10What should I send for a custom grappling shorts quotation?
Send your target quantity, size range, logo or artwork files, preferred colors, intended use and any labeling or packaging requirements.

Buyer FAQ

## Questions to resolve before ordering
Clear answers about specifications, customization, MOQ and sample approval.

01Are the black compression tights built into the MMA shorts?
No. The tight layer visible below the hem is a separate compression garment. This product is presented as an outer fight short; a built-in liner would require a separate 2-in-1 construction brief.
02What fabric and GSM do you recommend?
A four-way-stretch polyester-spandex woven direction around 130–180gsm can be evaluated for this short-cut style. Those values are a development range, not a verified specification; final composition, weight, stretch recovery and drying performance are confirmed using the chosen fabric and approved sample.
03Can the waistband include a hidden drawcord?
Yes, a hidden drawcord can be developed if required. The current photos verify the broad elastic waistband but do not prove an internal drawcord, so that detail must be specified and sampled.
04How can the logos be applied?
The waist branding appears as a sewn patch. The leg logo can be developed with a suitable heat-transfer, screen-print or silicone-print method depending on the artwork, fabric and required hand feel; the final process is confirmed before bulk production.
05Which activities are these shorts designed for?
The short cut and articulated crotch direction suit MMA, BJJ, Sanda, boxing, wrestling, combat training and high-intensity gym work. Final fit and movement should be approved on the sample.
06What is the MOQ and approval process?
Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. We align the fabric, fit, waist, reinforcement, branding, colors and size breakdown, then use the sample to approve the construction before bulk production.

Movement-First Design

## A combat short—not a tactical utility short
The construction prioritizes a secure waist, unrestricted leg movement and a smooth exterior rather than cargo storage.

01

### Fight-focused athletic cut
A short athletic profile with room through the thigh and no exposed storage pockets keeps the exterior clean for combat training.

02

### Stretch mobility
The polyester-spandex body moves through kicks, hip rotation, sprawls, squats and lunges.

03

### Triple waist control
Elastic support, a hook-and-loop fly and an internal drawcord work together for an adjustable hold.

04

### Reinforced split & hem
A short outer-leg opening releases the thigh while a reinforced hem with clean topstitching supports repeated high-mobility use.

05

### Smooth sublimation
Artwork is dyed into the synthetic fibers for complex graphics without a thick raised print layer.

06

### Panelled construction
Front, back, side and crotch panels shape the shorts around the hips, seat and upper leg.

Material & Construction

## Light, smooth and shaped for rotation

The lightweight woven body uses 88% polyester and 12% spandex to balance low weight, strength and stretch. Its smooth surface is suited to repeated training contact, while the short athletic cut, panelled shaping and side split reduce pull across the hip, crotch and thigh.
Fabric behavior
Lightweight stretch with a smooth hand and less water weight than bulky traditional satin constructions

Waist control
Elastic support plus hook-and-loop closure and an internal drawcord for adjustable security

Mobility
A reinforced short split creates extra clearance for kicks, knee strikes, lunges and deep squats

Hem finish
Reinforced hem construction with clean topstitching for a stable lower edge through repeated training

Panel shaping
Separated front, back, side and crotch areas follow the hips, seat and upper leg through rotation

Artwork
Sublimated graphics enter the synthetic fibers, avoiding a thick raised surface and reducing large-area cracking

Sample checks
Confirm abrasion, stretch recovery, seam strength, hook-and-loop comfort and logo color on the approved sample

Recommended Applications

## Combat training first, conditioning second
Designed around MMA and striking movement, with useful crossover into strength and high-intensity training.

### Combat training
MMA drills, BJJ No-Gi training, grappling movement, kickboxing, bag work, pad sessions and general martial-arts practice.

### Boxing fitness & conditioning
Boxing fitness, squats, lunges, mobility work, gym sessions and HIIT where a secure waist and free leg movement matter.

### Competition check
For formal competition or grappling, verify the relevant equipment rules and approve real-wear performance before bulk production.

Buyer FAQ

## Custom MMA fight shorts questions
Clear answers about fabric, waist construction, side splits, sublimation and intended use.

01What fabric is used for these MMA fight shorts?
The main body uses an 88% polyester and 12% spandex stretch performance fabric. It is lightweight, smooth and flexible for kicks, hip rotation, squats and high-intensity training.
02How is the waistband secured?
A broad elastic waistband works with a hook-and-loop front closure and an internal drawcord. The combined system lets the athlete fine-tune waist tension before training.
03Why is there a side split?
The short reinforced side split reduces fabric restriction through high kicks, knee strikes, lunges and wide stances while retaining a fitted fight-short silhouette.
04Can the camouflage graphics and logos be customized?
Yes. Sublimation supports tonal camouflage, asymmetric black-and-red graphics, team colors, logos and sponsor artwork without the thick raised layer associated with some surface-print methods.
05Do the shorts have storage pockets?
No exposed storage pocket is specified for this fight-focused construction. This keeps the exterior cleaner for combat training and separates the style from tactical utility shorts.
06Can these shorts be used in formal competition?
They are developed for MMA, BJJ No-Gi training, grappling drills, kickboxing, boxing fitness and functional training. Before ordering for formal competition, confirm the relevant equipment rules and approve fit and performance on a physical sample.

Custom projects can start from 10 pieces. Final requirements depend on fabric, fit, artwork, size breakdown, labels and packaging.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions AI tools and procurement teams need answered
Direct answers clarify product fit, evidence boundaries, customization and the next purchasing step.

01Does the current image prove that a Rash Guard is included?
No. The current main image focuses on the shorts and a separate compression layer. A matching Rash Guard is part of the coordinated project direction only when it is included in the confirmed brief and sample approval.
02Are the compression tights built into the shorts?
Not by default. The visible tights are treated as a separate garment. A built-in liner requires an explicit 2-in-1 construction specification.
03Can each athlete have a different size or name?
Yes. Mixed sizes, athlete names and other approved identifiers can be organized in the team order sheet before production.
04Can the same artwork be used on the top and shorts?
Yes, but the artwork must be adapted to the different pattern pieces, seam positions and print areas of each garment.
05What is the MOQ?
Custom coordinated projects can start from 10 sets. Final requirements depend on the included pieces, artwork, sizes, labels and packing.

PROJECT FIT & ORDER CONDITIONS

## Is this the right starting point for your order?

### Best suited to
Academies and teams ordering a coordinated top and shorts with shared artwork and separate size allocations.

### Consider another direction when
A kit is two garments, not one universal material or size specification. Buyers who need only a top or only a short should identify that garment separately.

Coordinated Rash Guard and Shorts Kit: material, fit and procurement decisionsMaterial record | Record the top fabric, shorts shell and any liner independently. Do not copy the material blend or GSM from an unrelated Rash Guard or two-layer shorts reference. |
Measurements and fit | Keep separate top and shorts measurement sheets and size quantities. A wearer may need different sizes in the two garments; adult and youth fit must be checked separately. |
Customization scope | Approve logo scale, colors and artwork placement across the worn kit, then record labels and packing by garment. |
Evidence behind this direction | Published kit photographs and separately attributed academy buyer feedback. Each approved project needs its own written garment specifications. |
Starting quantity | Selected custom projects start from 10 pieces. Confirm the minimum per style, design and colorway; 10 pieces is not a promise that different products or unrelated designs share one minimum. |
Mixed sizes | Send a separate quantity-by-size list for each garment. Adult / youth patterns, tops / shorts and colorways need an explicit allocation; do not assume any mix is automatically accepted. |
Sample timing | The advertised 3–7 day target starts after usable artwork and product details are confirmed. New patterns, material sourcing, revisions or special finishing can change the schedule. |
Quote scope | Request the unit and sample charges, artwork or development scope, labels, packaging, shipping basis and destination in one written quote. No universal price or free-sample entitlement is implied. |
Approval and repeat orders | Keep the approved sample version, artwork, materials, size chart, tolerances and packing instructions. Recheck material availability, MOQ and timing when reordering. |

BUYER QUESTIONS

## Frequently Asked Questions
Can we customize the samurai artwork and sleeve graphics?
Yes. Send your own artwork, logo placements and color references. TONTON reviews panel layout, print alignment and branding before sample approval. Artwork permissions and final files must be confirmed.
What are the fabric composition and GSM?
The supplied brief specifies a polyester/spandex compression blend, but does not confirm an exact percentage or fabric weight. Composition, GSM and tolerances are agreed for the selected material during sampling.
Is a silicone anti-slip hem included?
The supplied construction brief uses an extended torso with a double-needle bottom finish. Silicone is not confirmed for this garment; request a gripper separately if your project needs one.
What should we check on the sample?
Review shoulder movement, torso length, seam feel, stretch recovery, print alignment and appearance under stretch. Agree wash-test requirements and retain the approved sample for repeat orders.
What information is needed for a quote?
Send estimated quantity, size allocation, delivery country, target date, artwork and desired branding. Selected custom projects start from 10 pieces; minimums, sampling costs and timing are confirmed for your specification.

Page title: Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide | TONTON Sportswear

Home/Resources/Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning GuideTEAMWEAR SIZE & ORDER PLANNING

# Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide
Use the free team quantity planner to total rash guards and shorts by size, download a CSV and prepare a custom fightwear quote brief.
Reviewed November 18, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
Plan custom fightwear quantities from a confirmed member or customer list, not a universal size ratio. Record Rash Guard and shorts sizes separately, distinguish body measurements from finished-garment measurements, and check the selected pattern on a fit sample. Adult and youth fits need separate review. Any spare stock is an explicit purchasing decision, not an assumed allowance.

FREE TEAM ORDER TOOL

## Plan your rash guard and shorts quantities
Enter each garment separately. The size labels below are planning placeholders, not a TONTON measurement chart or a promise that every style offers every size. Keep adult, youth, different sleeve styles and colorways in separate plans.
Quantity by size label — no recommended size ratio is appliedSize label | Rash guards | Shorts |
XS | | |
S | | |
M | | |
L | | |
XL | | |
2XL | | |
3XL | | |
4XL | | |

0 Rash guards0 Shorts0 Total garment units
Equal totals do not confirm kit pairing. Check each member’s top and shorts size independently. MOQ, garment measurements and production timing still need project-specific confirmation.
Download CSVCopy quantity brief

Quantities are calculated in your browser and are not an order submission. Continuing opens an editable project brief; it does not send an inquiry.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Prepare the size information before ordering
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Fightwear Size & Quantity Planning Guide specification summaryBody measurements | Measurements taken on the wearer; identify the measuring points and units |
Garment measurements | Measurements taken on the selected garment laid flat, without stretching unless the method says otherwise |
Rash Guard size list | Quantity per approved top size and sleeve direction |
Shorts size list | Quantity per approved shorts size, cut and liner direction |
Youth requirements | Separate fit review and approved measurement chart; do not simply scale adult sizes |
Order approval | Confirm the chart version, quantities, units and permitted measurement tolerances with TONTON |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Known academy members | A named roster with an agreed fit reference | Collect top and shorts size independently; reconcile the order totals |
Retail collection | An independent brand allocating stock by style and size | Use your own sales or preorder evidence; no standard size ratio is assumed |
Adult and youth program | A club serving more than one fit group | Keep patterns, size lists and sample approvals separate |

ORDER PLANNING

## Worked example: 24 members, two separate size lists
Illustration only: these are invented order quantities for explaining the arithmetic, not a recommended size ratio or a TONTON size chart. Assume one Rash Guard and one pair of shorts per member, using size labels already confirmed for this example.

Worked example: 24 members, two separate size listsIllustrative size label | Rash Guards | Shorts |
XS | 2 | 1 |
S | 5 | 4 |
M | 8 | 9 |
L | 6 | 7 |
XL | 3 | 3 |
Total garment units | 24 | 24 |
The order contains 24 coordinated sets and 48 garment units. Top and shorts allocations differ because the same person may wear different sizes. List spares, extra tops, colorways or sleeve variants separately; confirm how MOQ applies to each actual order configuration.

01

## Use one measuring method and one unit system
For body measurements, follow the measuring points requested for the selected pattern, with the tape level and without pulling it tight. Record the intended close or relaxed fit alongside the measurements. For a reference garment, lay it flat and identify exactly where each width or length is measured.
Ask for the measurement chart and method for the actual style before converting member measurements into order sizes. Confirm whether a waist value is relaxed, stretched, flat width or circumference. Keep centimeters and inches clearly labeled and agree the tolerance before sample approval.

02

## Check the complete kit during movement

- Try the selected Rash Guard and shorts together on the intended wearer.

- Review reaching, rotation, sitting and squatting; check opacity and seam comfort under the intended fit.

- Check the Rash Guard hem, shorts waistband and liner together for unwanted overlap or pressure.

- Record the sample size and chart version, and resolve fit changes before collecting the final size allocation.

03

## Reconcile the roster before the order is approved
Use one row per wearer or one consolidated size list, then total each garment separately. Check sleeve variants, adult or youth groups, colors and any names or numbers against the approved artwork list. Remove duplicate member entries and keep personal details out of files that do not need them.
Mark the quantities as confirmed or still being collected. If you choose spare stock, state its sizes and quantity explicitly. TONTON reviews the applicable minimums and development requirements against the complete brief.

04

## Keep a clear record for new members and reorders
Retain the approved measurement chart, fit sample, style reference and artwork version. A reorder should specify what stays the same and which quantities or sizes change. Confirm material availability, color references, MOQ and schedule again rather than assuming an earlier order automatically sets the new terms.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- This guide is not a garment measurement chart or a recommendation to order fixed percentages in each size.

- A body chest circumference cannot be compared directly with a flat garment chest width. Even doubling a flat width does not determine the correct compression fit.

- One brand’s M, L or XL does not establish the equivalent size in a different pattern.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Can I download a team size allocation and use it in a quote request?
Yes. Enter rash guard and shorts quantities separately in the planner, download the CSV or copy the quantity brief, then continue to an editable Project Builder with the allocation included. This does not submit an order or confirm MOQ.
Does the planner select garment sizes for athletes?
No. It adds quantities entered against planning labels. Confirm the actual style size chart, available sizes, adult or youth pattern and sample fit before assigning a size to each wearer.
Should Rash Guards and shorts use the same size allocation?
Not automatically. Collect the top and shorts sizes separately because fit preferences and body proportions can differ. If you are ordering one set per member, both garment totals should match the member count, even when the size distribution differs.
Can I use another brand’s size chart?
Use it as a clearly identified reference only. Confirm the actual TONTON pattern, measuring method and sample fit before selecting order sizes; size labels are not universal.
Does this guide provide a TONTON size chart?
No. It explains measurement and quantity planning. Request the approved chart for the selected style, adult or youth fit and sample version before committing to dimensions or sizes.
How many garments are in an order for 24 matching sets?
If every set contains one Rash Guard and one pair of shorts, 24 sets contain 24 Rash Guards plus 24 pairs of shorts: 48 garment units. Extra garments and spares are counted separately.

Home/Resources/Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying GuideCOORDINATED FIGHTWEAR KIT PROCUREMENT

# Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying Guide
Plan a coordinated Rash Guard and shorts set: compare garment specifications, align artwork and colors, approve the worn kit and prepare a clear academy or private-label brief.
Reviewed October 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A custom Rash Guard and shorts kit is two garments developed as one coordinated project. Specify the fit, fabric and construction of each garment separately, then approve shared colors, artwork placement and the worn combination together. A matching graphic does not imply matching fabric, the same size label or identical order minimums.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Define both garments and their shared identity
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Custom Rash Guard & Shorts Team Kit Buying Guide specification summaryRash Guard | Sleeve length, fit, fabric direction, opacity, seams and lower-hem requirement |
Shorts | Length, side split, shell, liner option, waistband and intended use |
Shared artwork | Logo files, color references and placement approved on each garment |
Size allocation | Separate top and shorts size quantities, linked to the same kit program |
Branding and packing | Neck branding, labels, individual names and packing requirements when included |
Approval | Review both garments together; record artwork and specification versions separately |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
Academy uniform kit | A coordinated identity for members and training teams | Confirm top and shorts allocations, names and repeat-order records |
Private-label collection | A brand offering a coordinated Rash Guard and shorts range | Confirm fit, style variants, labels, packing and quantity by SKU |
High-split 2-in-1 shorts direction | Buyers comparing a high side opening with an inner layer | Inspect liner coverage, waistband comfort and the worn combination; review event requirements separately |

ORDER PLANNING

## Example brief: coordinated identity, separate specifications
This is a planning checklist, not a bundled SKU, fixed price or confirmed compatibility claim. The linked garments are reference directions; TONTON reviews the actual pairing on samples.

Example brief: coordinated identity, separate specificationsReview point | Rash Guard brief | Shorts brief |
Silhouette | Short or long sleeve; intended close fit | Leg length, side split and liner preference |
Material | Weight, composition, stretch and opacity for review | Shell and liner materials for review |
Artwork | Chest, sleeve and back placement | Leg panels, waistband and liner artwork where applicable |
Size order | Top quantity per approved size | Shorts quantity per approved size |
Worn sample | Hem control and upper-body movement | Waist security, liner coverage and leg movement |
Send a shared color reference and separate front/back artwork notes. Confirm material-specific color reproduction on physical samples, then approve the kit as a whole before bulk production.

01

## Start with the wearer and buying route
For an academy, define the members, adult or youth fit groups and whether the kit is for everyday training or a particular event. For a retail brand, define the target wearer, style count and intended collection identity. Use those requirements to choose the products rather than selecting a matching print first.

02

## Compare real product references before choosing the set
The Blue Team and White Pro Rash Guard pages provide published 220gsm product references, construction photographs and silicone lower-hem details. The High-Split 2-in-1 Grappling Shorts page shows a separate shorts construction with a high-split shell, inner layer and waistband details.
Use these pages to describe your preferred direction. Their individual evidence does not prove that a new pairing is already approved as a kit. Confirm the selected fabrics, measurements and worn combination on your project sample.

03

## Approve color and logo placement across both garments

- Use the same identified logo and artwork version for the kit.

- Specify color references and approve reproduction on each selected fabric.

- Review chest, sleeve, back and leg placements at the intended size and seam boundaries.

- Confirm how graphics meet at the waist and whether any artwork is hidden by the Rash Guard hem.

- Keep customer case photographs as production evidence; use your own permitted branding and artwork.

04

## Test the worn combination, then record the order
Review reaching, rotation and lower-body movement in the complete sample. Check the Rash Guard hem against the shorts waistband, liner coverage, skin-contact areas, opacity and seam comfort. Record changes separately for the top and shorts, then confirm the complete kit again if a change affects their interaction.
List the quantity per garment and size, labels, packing, delivery destination and target date. If each wearer receives one top and one pair of shorts, check that both garment totals agree; refer to the size and quantity guide for a worked example.

05

## Prepare the next production discussion
Send the style references, quantities, artwork status and destination through the Project Builder. TONTON reviews material options, sample requirements and the quotation scope before confirming the applicable MOQ and schedule. A coordinated kit does not imply a fixed package price or a guaranteed shared minimum across all variants.

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- A shared color name or screen image is not a physical color-approval standard across different materials.

- Do not apply a verified Rash Guard fabric composition to a shorts shell or liner.

- Do not treat an academy training kit as automatically compliant with a particular competition rule set.

BUYER FAQ

## Questions to confirm before approval

Can I order custom Rash Guards and shorts as a coordinated set?
Yes. Choose Coordinated Team Kit in the Project Builder and list both garments, size quantities, artwork and construction requirements. The project review and sample approval confirm the actual pairing.
Will matching colors look identical on different fabrics?
Do not assume so from a screen reference. Review the shared color target on the selected Rash Guard, shorts shell and liner materials, and agree the physical samples used for approval.
Can one top size be paired with a different shorts size?
Record the two size choices separately in your quantity list. Confirm the measurement charts, fit and any packing requirements for mixed-size sets before approving the order.
How is the price for a custom fightwear kit confirmed?
The quote depends on each garment’s material, construction, artwork, quantities, labels and packing, along with delivery requirements. Request a project-specific quote for the complete brief rather than inferring a kit price from a product photograph.

# Rash Guard Fabric & Construction Guide
A buyer guide to rash guard fabric weight, composition, opacity, stretch, sublimation and silicone anti-slip hems.
Reviewed September 15, 2026DIRECT ANSWER

## What buyers need to know
A dependable custom Rash Guard specification connects fabric weight, composition, opacity, stretch recovery, seam construction and hem control. Selected TONTON styles use 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra; the Blue Team and White Pro Club examples use 85% polyester and 15% spandex with a silicone anti-slip elastic band.

REAL PRODUCT & PROCESS EVIDENCE

## Inspect the material, construction and workflow
Original product or production photos support the specification. No generated product imagery is used.

01Stretch fabric surface and multi-row seam construction on the real sample.

02Breathable mesh inset with a clean stitched transition between panels.

03Reinforced seam intersection at a high-movement panel junction.

SPECIFICATION SNAPSHOT

## Confirmed details at a glance
Use this table as a starting point. Final product details are confirmed against the selected style and approved sample.

Rash Guard Fabric & Construction Guide specification summaryExample fabric weight | 220gsm ultra-fine Lycra |
Verified composition | 85% polyester / 15% spandex on selected styles |
Coverage direction | Opaque under stretch; reconfirmed on the approved sample |
Decoration | Sublimation-ready panel artwork |
Hem option | Silicone anti-slip elastic band |
Typical use | BJJ, MMA, grappling and team training |

BUYER DECISION TABLE

## Match the specification to the intended use

Buyer decision comparisonOption | Best suited to | Confirm before approval |
220gsm ultra-fine Lycra | Buyers prioritizing soft hand feel, strong stretch and opaque coverage | Confirm opacity, recovery and fit on the approved sample |
85% polyester / 15% spandex | Sublimated team graphics on selected verified styles | Confirm the composition belongs to the selected style |
Silicone anti-slip hem | Close-fit training where lower-hem movement needs more control | Review grip feel and placement during movement |

01

## Why fabric weight and opacity should be reviewed together
Fabric weight alone does not confirm how a garment performs when stretched. Buyers should review weight, hand feel, recovery and opacity on the same approved sample, under the intended fit direction.

02

## What the polyester-spandex blend contributes
On the verified 85/15 styles, polyester provides a smooth surface suited to sublimated graphics, while spandex provides the stretch required for a close performance fit.

03

## Construction details worth specifying

- Sleeve length and raglan panel direction

- Seam placement and stretch compatibility

- Lower-hem grip requirement

- Logo, sponsor mark and panel-artwork positions

- Size range, fit direction, private labels and packaging

WHEN NOT TO USE THIS DIRECTION

## Limits buyers should confirm

- Do not select a fabric from GSM alone; weight does not prove opacity, recovery or comfort.

- Do not assume every TONTON Rash Guard uses the same composition or hem construction.

- Do not approve bulk production before checking the intended fit and artwork on the physical sample.
